## Appendix C — API contract (`@acme/report-plugin-api`, 1.0.0-rc.1)

```ts
import type { RecordBatch, Table } from "apache-arrow"; // Arrow major is pinned by the SDK; changing it is an API major

// ── Primitives ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
export type Awaitable<T> = T | Promise<T>;
export type JsonValue = string | number | boolean | null | JsonValue[] | { [key: string]: JsonValue };
/** Open enum: 1.x minors may add values. Plugins MUST handle unknown values. */
export type Open<T extends string> = T | (string & {});
export interface Disposable { dispose(): Awaitable<void>; }
export interface PageRequest { cursor?: string; limit: number; }
export interface Page<T> { items: T[]; nextCursor?: string; }

// ── Entry module: lifecycle hooks ───────────────────────────────────────────
export interface PluginModule {
  /** load — must register a handler for every contribution declared in the manifest, and nothing else. */
  activate(ctx: PluginContext): Awaitable<void>;
  /** unload — at most once; NOT called after crashes. Never rely on it for durability. */
  deactivate?(reason: DeactivationReason): Awaitable<void>;
  /** reload — called on the outgoing instance. ≤5 s, ≤1 MiB. Best effort; used only to keep caches warm. */
  snapshotState?(): Awaitable<StateSnapshot | undefined>;
  /** reload — called on the incoming instance after activate(). snapshot.stateVersion may be older. */
  restoreState?(snapshot: StateSnapshot): Awaitable<"restored" | "discarded">;
  /** Return "applied" to avoid a restart. */
  onConfigurationChanged?(change: { previous: JsonValue; current: JsonValue }): Awaitable<"applied" | "restartRequired">;
}
export type DeactivationReason = Open<
  "disabled" | "uninstalled" | "idle" | "reload" | "upgrade" | "rollback" | "hostShutdown" | "dependencyUnavailable" | "grantsChanged"
>;
export interface StateSnapshot { stateVersion: number; data: JsonValue; }

// ── Context ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
export interface PluginContext {
  readonly plugin: { id: string; version: string; installationId: string; /** absent when isolation is "shared" */ tenantId?: string };
  readonly host: HostInfo;
  readonly log: Logger;
  readonly metrics: Metrics;
  readonly config: { get<T = JsonValue>(): T };
  readonly register: Registrar;
  /** Disposed automatically after deactivate(). */
  readonly subscriptions: { add(d: Disposable): void };
  /** Each of these throws CAPABILITY_NOT_GRANTED when its capability isn't granted. */
  readonly storage: KeyValueStore;
  readonly secrets: SecretStore;
  readonly http: HttpClient;
  readonly reports: ReportsApi;
  /** @experimental "services" */
  readonly services: ServiceRegistry;
}
export interface HostInfo {
  readonly version: string;
  /** Highest API version this host supports. */
  readonly apiVersion: string;
  readonly environment: Open<"production" | "staging" | "development">;
  supports(feature: string): boolean;
}
export interface InvocationContext {
  readonly requestId: string;
  readonly tenantId: string;
  readonly principal: Principal;
  readonly locale: string;
  readonly timeZone: string;
  /** Epoch ms. Broker calls made during this invocation inherit it. */
  readonly deadline: number;
  readonly signal: AbortSignal;
  /** Pre-tagged with requestId and traceId. */
  readonly log: Logger;
}
export type Principal =
  | { kind: "user"; userId: string; displayName: string; email?: string; groups?: string[] }
  | { kind: "installation"; installationId: string };

export interface Logger {
  debug(message: string, fields?: Record<string, JsonValue>): void;
  info(message: string, fields?: Record<string, JsonValue>): void;
  warn(message: string, fields?: Record<string, JsonValue>): void;
  error(message: string, fields?: Record<string, JsonValue>, error?: unknown): void;
}
export interface Metrics {
  counter(name: string, labels?: Record<string, string>): { add(n?: number): void };
  histogram(name: string, labels?: Record<string, string>): { record(value: number): void };
  gauge(name: string, labels?: Record<string, string>): { set(value: number): void };
}

export interface Registrar {
  dataSource(id: string, impl: DataSourceProvider): Disposable;
  transform(id: string, impl: TransformProvider): Disposable;
  visualization(id: string, impl: VisualizationBackend): Disposable;
  exporter(id: string, impl: ExporterProvider): Disposable;
  command(id: string, impl: CommandHandler): Disposable;
  eventSubscription(id: string, impl: EventHandler): Disposable;
  /** @experimental "services" */
  service(serviceId: string, impl: ServiceImplementation): Disposable;
}

// ── Brokered capabilities ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
export interface KeyValueStore {
  get(key: string): Promise<{ value: JsonValue; revision: string } | undefined>;
  /** ifRevision: null = only if the key is absent; a string = only if unchanged. A mismatch throws CONFLICT. */
  set(key: string, value: JsonValue, opts?: { ifRevision?: string | null }): Promise<{ revision: string }>;
  delete(key: string, opts?: { ifRevision?: string }): Promise<void>;
  list(opts?: { prefix?: string } & Partial<PageRequest>): Promise<Page<string>>;
}
declare const secretRefBrand: unique symbol;
/** Opaque. The broker substitutes the value; the plaintext never enters plugin memory. */
export interface SecretRef { readonly [secretRefBrand]: true; }
export interface SecretStore {
  /** template, e.g. "Bearer {}" */
  ref(name: string, template?: string): SecretRef;
  /** Requires access: "read". Audited. */
  read(name: string): Promise<string>;
}
export interface HttpClient { fetch(request: HttpRequest, opts?: { signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<HttpResponse>; }
export interface HttpRequest {
  /** https only; the host must be allowlisted in capabilities.network */
  url: string;
  method?: "GET" | "HEAD" | "POST" | "PUT" | "PATCH" | "DELETE";
  headers?: Record<string, string | SecretRef>;
  query?: Record<string, string | SecretRef>;
  body?: string | Uint8Array | { json: JsonValue };
  timeoutMs?: number;
  maxResponseBytes?: number;
}
export interface HttpResponse {
  readonly status: number;
  readonly headers: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
  bytes(): Promise<Uint8Array>;
  text(): Promise<string>;
  json<T = JsonValue>(): Promise<T>;
  body(): AsyncIterable<Uint8Array>;
}
/** Every call runs on behalf of on.principal. */
export interface ReportsApi {
  get(on: InvocationContext, reportId: string): Promise<ReportSummary>;
  list(on: InvocationContext, query?: { folderId?: string } & Partial<PageRequest>): Promise<Page<ReportSummary>>;
  getDefinition(on: InvocationContext, reportId: string): Promise<ReportDefinition>;
  /** Requires reports: "readWrite". */
  updateMetadata(on: InvocationContext, reportId: string, patch: { description?: string; tags?: string[] }): Promise<ReportSummary>;
}
export interface ReportSummary { id: string; title: string; folderId?: string; ownerId: string; tags: string[]; updatedAt: string; publishedAt?: string; }
export interface ReportDefinition extends ReportSummary { pages: Array<{ id: string; title?: string; elements: ElementRef[] }>; }
export interface ElementRef {
  id: string;
  /** FQID, or "builtin:<kind>" */
  contribution: string;
  options: JsonValue;
  optionsVersion: number;
}

/** @experimental "services" */
export interface ServiceRegistry { get(serviceId: string): ServiceClient | undefined; }
export interface ServiceClient { readonly version: string; call<R = JsonValue>(on: InvocationContext, method: string, params: JsonValue): Promise<R>; }
export type ServiceImplementation = Record<string, (params: JsonValue, inv: InvocationContext & { callerPluginId: string }) => Awaitable<JsonValue>>;

// ── Datasets ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
export type FieldType = Open<"string" | "integer" | "decimal" | "float" | "boolean" | "date" | "timestamp" | "duration">;
export interface Field {
  name: string;
  type: FieldType;
  nullable: boolean;
  displayName?: string;
  semanticType?: Open<"currency" | "percent" | "geo.country" | "geo.region" | "geo.latlon" | "url" | "email" | "identifier">;
  format?: string;
  decimal?: { precision: number; scale: number };
  timeZone?: string;
}
export interface Schema { fields: Field[]; }
export type ScalarValue = string | number | boolean | null | { int64: string } | { decimal: string } | { date: string } | { timestamp: string };
export type Row = Record<string, ScalarValue>;
/** Plain Row[] batches are converted to Arrow by the SDK. */
export interface DatasetSource { schema: Schema; batches: AsyncIterable<RecordBatch | Row[]>; }
export interface DatasetStream extends AsyncIterable<RecordBatch> { readonly schema: Schema; }

/** The host sends only ops the manifest lists in pushdown.filterOps, so new ops in a minor are safe. */
export type Predicate =
  | { op: "and" | "or"; args: Predicate[] }
  | { op: "not"; arg: Predicate }
  | { op: "eq" | "neq" | "lt" | "lte" | "gt" | "gte"; field: string; value: ScalarValue }
  | { op: "in"; field: string; values: ScalarValue[] }
  | { op: "between"; field: string; low: ScalarValue; high: ScalarValue }
  | { op: "isNull" | "isNotNull"; field: string }
  | { op: "contains" | "startsWith" | "endsWith"; field: string; value: string; caseSensitive: boolean };
export type AggregateFn = "count" | "countDistinct" | "sum" | "avg" | "min" | "max";

// ── Data source ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
export interface ConnectionConfig { readonly id: string; readonly values: Readonly<Record<string, JsonValue | SecretRef>>; }
export interface ObjectRef { path: string[]; }
export interface ObjectInfo { ref: ObjectRef; displayName: string; kind: Open<"folder" | "table" | "view" | "query">; hasChildren: boolean; }
export interface ValidationIssue { path: string; message: string; severity: "error" | "warning"; }
export interface QueryRequest {
  connection: ConnectionConfig;
  object: ObjectRef;
  fields: string[];
  filter?: Predicate;
  sort?: Array<{ field: string; direction: "asc" | "desc"; nulls: "first" | "last" }>;
  limit?: number;
  aggregation?: { groupBy: string[]; measures: Array<{ as: string; fn: AggregateFn; field?: string }> };
}
export interface QueryResult extends DatasetSource {
  /** What the source ACTUALLY applied; the host applies the rest. Must be exact for limit and aggregation. aggregation ⇒ filter. */
  applied: { projection: boolean; filter: boolean; sort: boolean; limit: boolean; aggregation: boolean };
}
export interface DataSourceProvider {
  validateConnection?(conn: ConnectionConfig, inv: InvocationContext): Awaitable<ValidationIssue[]>;
  testConnection(conn: ConnectionConfig, inv: InvocationContext): Promise<{ ok: boolean; message?: string }>;
  listObjects?(conn: ConnectionConfig, parent: ObjectRef | null, page: PageRequest, inv: InvocationContext): Promise<Page<ObjectInfo>>;
  getSchema(conn: ConnectionConfig, object: ObjectRef, inv: InvocationContext): Promise<Schema>;
  query(request: QueryRequest, inv: InvocationContext): Promise<QueryResult>;
}

// ── Transform ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
export interface TransformProvider {
  /** Pure; ≤1 s; called at design time. */
  outputSchema(inputs: Schema[], params: JsonValue, inv: InvocationContext): Awaitable<Schema>;
  execute(inputs: DatasetStream[], params: JsonValue, inv: InvocationContext): Awaitable<DatasetSource>;
}

// ── Visualization (backend side) ────────────────────────────────────────────
export interface VisualizationBackend {
  /** Pure, deterministic, idempotent. Migrates fromVersion → the manifest's optionsVersion. */
  migrateOptions?(options: JsonValue, fromVersion: number): Awaitable<JsonValue>;
  /** Called from the UI via host.invokeBackend(). */
  methods?: Record<string, (params: JsonValue, inv: InvocationContext) => Awaitable<JsonValue>>;
}

// ── Visualization (UI side; @acme/report-plugin-ui, runs in the sandboxed iframe) ──
export interface VisualizationView {
  mount(root: HTMLElement, init: ViewUpdate & { host: ViewHost }): Awaitable<void>;
  update(update: ViewUpdate): Awaitable<void>;
  unmount?(): Awaitable<void>;
  toImage?(format: "png" | "svg", size: { width: number; height: number }): Promise<Blob>;
}
export interface ViewUpdate {
  changed: ReadonlyArray<Open<"data" | "options" | "size" | "theme" | "locale">>;
  /** roles: role id → column names */
  data: { table: Table; roles: Readonly<Record<string, string[]>> };
  options: JsonValue;
  size: { width: number; height: number };
  theme: { mode: Open<"light" | "dark">; tokens: Readonly<Record<string, string>> };
  locale: string;
  timeZone: string;
}
export interface ViewHost {
  emit(event: ViewEvent): void;
  invokeBackend<R = JsonValue>(method: string, params: JsonValue): Promise<R>;
  readonly log: Logger;
}
export type ViewEvent =
  | { type: "rendered" }
  | { type: "selection"; filter: Predicate | null }
  | { type: "drilldown"; field: string; value: ScalarValue }
  | { type: "error"; userMessage: string };

// ── Exporter ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
export interface ExporterProvider {
  migrateOptions?(options: JsonValue, fromVersion: number): Awaitable<JsonValue>;
  export(job: ExportJob, sink: ByteSink, inv: InvocationContext): Promise<{ fileName?: string }>;
}
export interface ExportJob { format: string; options: JsonValue; report: ReportSnapshot; }
export interface ReportSnapshot { report: ReportSummary; pages: Array<{ id: string; title?: string; elements: SnapshotElement[] }>; }
export interface SnapshotElement {
  id: string;
  contribution: string;
  title?: string;
  layout: { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number };
  /** Present when needs includes "data". Already filtered by row-level security. */
  data?(): Promise<DatasetStream>;
  /** Present when needs includes "images". */
  image?(format: "png" | "svg"): Promise<Uint8Array>;
}
export interface ByteSink { write(chunk: Uint8Array): Promise<void>; readonly bytesWritten: number; }

// ── Commands and events ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
export interface CommandHandler { execute(args: CommandArgs, inv: InvocationContext): Promise<CommandResult>; }
export interface CommandArgs { context: Open<"global" | "report" | "dataset">; reportId?: string; datasetId?: string; input?: JsonValue; }
export interface CommandResult {
  message?: string;
  refresh?: boolean;
  /** Must be an allowlisted host or the app itself. */
  openUrl?: string;
}

export interface EventHandler { handle(event: HostEvent, inv: InvocationContext): Promise<void | EventVerdict>; }
export interface HostEvent<T = JsonValue> {
  /** Use for deduplication; delivery is at least once. */
  id: string;
  type: Open<"report.published" | "report.deleted" | "dataset.refreshed" | "schedule.delivered" | "installation.configured" | "report.beforePublish">;
  occurredAt: string;
  subject: { kind: Open<"report" | "dataset" | "schedule" | "installation">; id: string };
  attempt: number;
  data: T;
}
/** @experimental "events.veto" — honored only for report.beforePublish; fails open after 2 s. */
export type EventVerdict = { allow: true } | { allow: false; userMessage: string };

// ── Errors ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
export type ErrorCode = Open<
  | "INVALID_ARGUMENT" | "NOT_FOUND" | "PERMISSION_DENIED" | "CAPABILITY_NOT_GRANTED"
  | "UNDECLARED_CONTRIBUTION" | "MISSING_CONTRIBUTION" | "EXPERIMENTAL_NOT_ENABLED" | "CONFLICT"
  | "FAILED_PRECONDITION" | "RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED" | "TIMEOUT" | "CANCELLED" | "UNAVAILABLE"
  | "PLUGIN_CRASHED" | "INCOMPATIBLE_API" | "SANDBOX_VIOLATION" | "INTERNAL"
>;
export declare class PluginError extends Error {
  constructor(code: ErrorCode, message: string, init?: { retryable?: boolean; userMessage?: string; details?: JsonValue; cause?: unknown });
  readonly code: ErrorCode;
  readonly retryable: boolean;
  readonly userMessage?: string;
  readonly details?: JsonValue;
}

// ── SDK helpers (@acme/report-plugin-sdk) ───────────────────────────────────
export declare function definePlugin(module: PluginModule): PluginModule;
export declare function defineMigrations(
  steps: Record<number, (options: JsonValue) => JsonValue>
): (options: JsonValue, fromVersion: number) => JsonValue;
```

## 0. Assumptions (confirm before freeze)

There was no existing code to anchor this to, so the design assumes the following. If any of these is wrong, Sections 8 (sandbox) and 9 (API contract) change the most.

- **A1:** The report host runs server-side. Plugins run as **separate processes**, so the host language doesn't limit what plugins can be written in. At launch there are official SDKs for **TypeScript (Node 22)** and **Python 3.12**.
- **A2:** Production runs on Linux containers (Kubernetes). Development happens on Windows, macOS and Linux.
- **A3:** The product is multi-tenant, and report data is confidential to each tenant.
- **A4:** Plugin authors are internal teams. We still design for a plugin that is *buggy or compromised*, not one that is *benign*. The same boundary lets us admit third parties later.
- **A5:** A report is a pipeline: **fetch data → transform → visualize → export/deliver**.

---

## 1. Goals and non-goals

**Goals**

1. Teams build, test, publish, and roll back plugins on their own schedule, without a host release.
2. A failing plugin (crash, hang, leak, or malicious code) cannot affect the host, other plugins, or other tenants.
3. The host API can change without breaking published plugins. When a breaking change is needed, it is scheduled, visible, and supported by tooling.
4. Saved reports keep working across plugin upgrades, including when a plugin's config format changes.
5. Upgrades cause no downtime, and a rollback takes one action.
6. Plugin code written against the local dev harness runs unchanged in production.

**Non-goals for v1**

- A public marketplace or third-party authors. The architecture allows it, but the process and tooling don't exist yet.
- In-process plugins of any kind (see §8.2).
- Direct plugin-to-plugin communication. Only host-brokered services are allowed (§4.6).
- Plugins that change host UI outside the defined visualization slots.

---

## 2. Architecture overview

```
 rpt-plugin CLI --(signed bundle)--> +------------------------ Core host (report service) ------------------------+
                                     |                                                                             |
                                     |  Plugin Catalog -------> Runtime Registry -------> Contribution Index      |
                                     |  (versions, signatures,   (desired-state            ("pluginId/contrib"    |
                                     |   approvals, rollouts)     reconciler)               -> plugin@version)    |
                                     |                                                                             |
                                     |  Report Engine --invoke--> Invocation Router       Capability Broker      |
                                     |                            (breaker, limits,       (implements            |
                                     |                             token minting)          HostServices)          |
                                     +-------------------------------|-----------------------------^---------------+
                                                                     | gRPC / mTLS                 | gRPC / mTLS
                                     +-------------------------------v------ Plugin Runner node ---|---------------+
                                     |  Supervisor: spawn, health-check, drain, kill, report state                 |
                                     |   +------ sandbox ---------------+   +------ sandbox ---------------+       |
                                     |   | ledger-connector@2.3.1 / T1  |   | fx-rates@1.0.4 / T1          |  ...  |
                                     |   | SDK <-UDS-> supervisor proxy |   | SDK <-UDS-> supervisor proxy |       |
                                     |   +------------------------------+   +------------------------------+       |
                                     +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+

 Browser: client-side visualization bundles run in sandboxed, cross-origin iframes. The host UI sends them data over postMessage.
```

| Component | Responsibility | State owner |
|---|---|---|
| **Plugin Catalog** | Stores published plugin versions: bundle, manifest, signature, SBOM, review status, per-tenant enablement, pins, and rollouts. It is the source of truth for *what may run*. | Catalog DB + object storage |
| **Runtime Registry** | A reconciler. It compares desired instances (from the catalog and resolution) with actual instances (reported by runners) and sends Start, Drain and Stop commands. It is the only component allowed to decide state transitions. | Desired state lives in the DB; actual state is owned by the runner supervisor |
| **Contribution Index** | Maps `pluginId/contributionId` to the resolved version and its manifest entry. It is built **from manifests only**, so no plugin code runs to list or authorize contributions. | Derived and cached |
| **Invocation Router** | Picks or starts an instance, applies deadlines, concurrency limits and circuit breakers, mints invocation tokens, and retries under a policy. | Stateless |
| **Capability Broker** | Implements `HostServices`, the plugin's only path to I/O. It authorizes every call. | Stateless, with an audit log |
| **Plugin Runner** | A separate deployment on a dedicated node pool. Its supervisor runs the sandboxes. | Instance state |

**Why runners are separate from the core host:** a fork bomb, memory blow-up, or sandbox escape hits the runner nodes, not the report API nodes. It also lets runners scale on their own, and their nodes can have a stricter security profile (gVisor runtime class, no cloud credentials). In local development, `rpt-plugin dev` runs the host and a supervisor together in one process.

## 3. Terminology

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Plugin** | A named, versioned bundle, identified by `id` plus a semver `version`. |
| **Extension point** | A slot defined by the host with a typed contract: `dataSource`, `transform`, `visualization`, `exporter`, `action`, `service`. |
| **Contribution** | One thing a plugin provides at an extension point. Referenced as `pluginId/contributionId`. |
| **Instance** | A running sandbox for one `(pluginId, version, tenantId)`. |
| **Invocation** | One call from host to plugin. It carries a context, a deadline, a principal, and a short-lived token. |
| **Host API version** | The version of the plugin contract, as `MAJOR.MINOR`. It is independent of the product's release version. |
| **Plugin config** | Settings per tenant for a plugin, set by a tenant admin (for example region or account ID). |
| **Contribution config** | Settings for each use of a contribution, set by a report author and saved inside the report. |

## 4. Extension points

Every contribution declares:

- **`configSchema`**: a JSON Schema (2020-12) file in the bundle. The host renders the config form from it and **validates config before every invocation**, so plugins only ever receive valid config.
- **`configVersion`**: an integer. Increment it whenever `configSchema` changes in a way older saved config doesn't satisfy. The host calls `MigrateConfig` to upgrade saved config (§7.7).

| Kind | Purpose | Plugin implements (proto service) | Invoked when |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dataSource` | Connect to a data system | `DataSourceService`: `Describe`, `TestConnection`, `Query` (streams Arrow) | Dataset browsing, preview, report run |
| `transform` | Reshape tabular data | `TransformService`: `ResolveOutputSchema`, `Apply` (bidirectional stream) | A pipeline step |
| `visualization` | Render a chart or table | `VisualizationService.Render` on the server, and/or a client web bundle | Viewing, PDF/email export |
| `exporter` | Produce a file | `ExporterService.Export` (streams bytes) | Download, scheduled delivery |
| `action` | React to host events | `ActionService.HandleEvent` | `report.generated`, `schedule.failed`, … |
| `service` | Shared function for other plugins | `ServiceContribution.Invoke` | A brokered call from another plugin |

### 4.1 dataSource

- **Capabilities** (declared in the manifest): `filterPushdown`, `projectionPushdown`, `limitPushdown`, `incremental`, `sampling`, plus the list of `filterFunctions` the source can push down.
- **`Query` request:** dataset, projected columns, filters as a portable expression AST (`Expression` in `common.proto`), limit, and an incremental cursor.
- **`Query` response stream:** Arrow schema first, then record batches of **≤ 4 MiB** each, then a final `QueryComplete` with `applied_filter_ids`, `limit_applied`, `next_cursor`, and `row_count`.
- **Correctness never depends on pushdown.** The host re-applies every filter the plugin didn't list in `applied_filter_ids`, and every limit not marked applied. A plugin that pushes down nothing is slow but still correct.
- The host enforces tenant row and byte caps on the stream. If a batch doesn't match the declared schema, the invocation fails with `INTERNAL`.

### 4.2 transform

- `ResolveOutputSchema(inputs, config)` must be cheap and must not depend on data. The report editor calls it to type-check pipelines.
- `Apply` receives named input streams and returns one output stream matching the resolved schema.
- Transforms are assumed **deterministic**, and the host may cache results by `(plugin@version, config, input hashes)`. If a transform isn't, it declares `deterministic: false`.

### 4.3 visualization

- **Server render** (required for PDF and email export): the input is Arrow data, contribution config, a format (`svg | png | html_static`), size, device pixel ratio, theme tokens, locale and time zone. The output is a content stream plus a header with `mime_type` and required `alt_text`.
- **Client render** (optional, for interactive views): the manifest points `client.entry` at an ES module. It's loaded in a sandboxed iframe (§8.2, layer 7) and speaks the `client-viz/1` postMessage protocol:
  - host → plugin: `init {apiVersion, theme, locale}`, `render {data: ArrowIPC bytes, config, size}`, `resize`, `dispose`
  - plugin → host: `ready {protocolVersion}`, `rendered`, `interaction {kind: "select" | "drilldown", payload}` (payload is validated against the manifest's `interactionSchema`), `error {reason, userMessage}`
  - The bundle has no network, no storage and no host cookies.
- The server and client renderings of the same config should look the same. This is a guideline, not something the host enforces.

### 4.4 exporter

- The input is the host's **report document model**, a stream of `ReportDocumentPart`s: metadata, headings, paragraphs, tables (Arrow chunks), images (already rendered by visualizations), and page breaks.
- Exporters **never call visualizations directly**. The host renders every block first, which keeps exporters simple and makes sandbox call graphs shallow.
- The output is an `ExportHeader {mime_type, file_name}` followed by content bytes. `mime_type` must be one the manifest declares for that format.

### 4.5 action

- Event types come from a versioned catalog that ships with the host API (§9). Payload JSON Schemas are published alongside the proto.
- Delivery is **at least once**. `event_id` is the idempotency key, and plugins must be idempotent.
- The host retries with exponential backoff, up to `delivery.maxAttempts` (default 8) or 24 hours. After that the event goes to a dead-letter queue, visible to tenant admins, who can replay it.
- Large artifacts, such as a generated PDF, are passed by handle and fetched with `HostServices.GetArtifact`. This requires the `reports:read` scope.

### 4.6 service (plugin-to-plugin)

- The provider declares `services[]` with its own `version` (semver) and methods, each with request and response JSON Schemas.
- The consumer declares `dependencies.services[]` with a `ref` (`pluginId/serviceId`), a version range, and `optional`.
- The consumer calls `HostServices.InvokeService`. The broker then:
  1. rejects the call unless the service is in the consumer's manifest dependencies;
  2. validates the request against the schema;
  3. invokes the provider **under the original invocation's principal** (see §8.3 on the confused deputy);
  4. validates the response.
- Call depth is capped at 3, and cycles are rejected at resolution time.
- There are no shared objects, callbacks, or streams across plugins in v1.

## 5. Manifest

Every bundle has `plugin.json` at its root. The **normative schema** is `schemas/plugin-manifest.v1.schema.json`, and a full example is in `examples/ledger-connector/plugin.json`.

### 5.1 Top-level fields

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `manifestVersion` | yes | `1`. This versions the *file format* and changes separately from `api.version`. |
| `id` | yes | Reverse-DNS, lowercase, e.g. `com.example.finance.ledger-connector`. The namespace prefix `com.example.<team>` is bound to the owning team in the catalog. |
| `version` | yes | SemVer 2.0. Must be greater than every version already published. |
| `displayName`, `description`, `icon`, `repository` | `displayName` | Shown in the UI. |
| `owner` | yes | `team`, `contact`, `oncall` (pager service). The quarantine alerts in §7.6 go here. |
| `api` | yes | `version`: one or more caret ranges, e.g. `"^1.2"` or `"^1.4 \|\| ^2.0"`. `proposed`: preview API names (§9.5). |
| `runtime` | yes | `type` (`node` / `python` / `wasm` (reserved)), `version`, `entry`. |
| `activation` | no | Activation events (§7.3). Defaults to every declared contribution. |
| `lifecycle` | no | `activateTimeoutMs`, `idleTimeoutSec`, `drainTimeoutSec`, `supportsLiveConfig`, `stateSchemaVersion`. |
| `configSchema` | no | JSON Schema for plugin config (per tenant). Secrets never go here (see `permissions.secrets`). |
| `contributes` | yes | `dataSources`, `transforms`, `visualizations`, `exporters`, `actions`, `services`. At least one entry in total. |
| `permissions` | no | `network`, `secrets`, `data`, `storage` (§8.3). An absent field means no access. |
| `resources` | no | Resource requests, bounded by §8.4. |
| `dependencies` | no | `services[]` (§4.6). |

### 5.2 Semantic validation (beyond JSON Schema, run by `rpt-plugin validate` and at publish)

1. The `id` namespace belongs to the publishing team's CI identity.
2. `version` is greater than the latest published version for this `id`.
3. Contribution IDs are unique within each kind, and service IDs are unique.
4. Every `onContribution:`, `onEvent:` and `onService:` activation event refers to something declared.
5. Every file path exists in the bundle, is a relative path inside the bundle (no `..`), and every referenced JSON Schema is itself valid 2020-12.
6. `api.version` overlaps the versions the host currently supports.
7. `api.proposed` is non-empty only when publishing to the `canary` channel.
8. `resources` are within the no-approval ceiling unless the platform has approved an override for the plugin.
9. **Upgrade diff against the previous published version:**

| Change | Requirement |
|---|---|
| A contribution or service is removed | Plugin **major** bump |
| `configSchema` rejects previously valid config | `configVersion` bump plus a migration fixture, checked by conformance (§9.7) |
| A service method is removed or its schema becomes incompatible | Service `version` major bump **and** plugin major bump |
| `permissions` gain anything | Allowed, but the version is **held per tenant until an admin approves** (§6.3, step 2) |
| `resources` go above the no-approval ceiling | Platform approval |
| `api.version` drops a major the previous version supported | Plugin major bump |

### 5.3 Why the manifest is static

Contributions, permissions and activation events are plain data. They are never computed at runtime. This lets the host list, index, authorize, diff, and show permission prompts **without running plugin code**. It also makes lazy activation possible, and means the publish diff checker can enforce §5.2.9. At activation, the host rejects any contribution the plugin registers that the manifest doesn't declare, and fails activation if a declared one isn't registered.

## 6. Registry

### 6.1 Catalog data model

```
plugin              (id PK, owner_team, status[active|deprecated|blocked], created_at)
plugin_version      (plugin_id, version, manifest_json, bundle_uri, bundle_sha256, signature_bundle,
                     sbom_uri, api_ranges, published_by, published_at,
                     status[pending_checks|published|yanked|blocked], conformance_report_uri)
tenant_plugin       (tenant_id, plugin_id, enabled, channel[stable|canary], pinned_version NULL,
                     plugin_config_json, config_revision)
permission_approval (tenant_id, plugin_id, permissions_hash, approved_by, approved_at)
rollout             (plugin_id, version, channel, stage, percent, stage_started_at, paused,
                     policy_json)                                   -- see 6.6
instance_directory  (instance_id, plugin_id, version, tenant_id, runner_node, state, updated_at) -- written by runners
contribution_usage  (report_id, tenant_id, contribution_ref, plugin_major, config_version)       -- blast radius
resolution          (resolution_id PK = hash(tenant, {pluginId->version}), tenant_id, created_at)
```

### 6.2 Publish pipeline

1. **Pack.** `rpt-plugin pack` produces `bundle.tar.zst` containing `plugin.json`, the built code, a lockfile, vendored dependencies, and a CycloneDX SBOM.
2. **Sign.** Signing is keyless (Sigstore), done in the team's CI. The OIDC identity must match the CI workflow registered for the owning team.
3. **Upload and static checks.** The catalog verifies the signature and digest, the JSON Schema, the §5.2 semantic rules and upgrade diff, and the size limit (≤ 200 MiB). It scans the SBOM and blocks critical CVEs that have a known exploit.
4. **Conformance.** The catalog starts the bundle in a staging runner and runs the conformance kit (§9.7) at every API version the plugin claims.
5. **Published.** The version enters its channel's rollout (§6.6). Failures at steps 3 and 4 return a machine-readable report to the CLI.

Runners **re-verify the signature and digest before every sandbox start**. This protects against tampering in the catalog's storage.

### 6.3 Resolution (per tenant, deterministic)

The inputs are the tenant's enabled plugins, their channel or pin, and the catalog.

1. **Choose a candidate** for each plugin. A pinned version wins. Otherwise take the newest `published` version on the tenant's channel whose rollout stage includes this tenant.
2. **Filter candidates.** Drop versions whose API ranges don't overlap the host's supported versions, versions that are `yanked` or `blocked`, and versions whose **`permissions_hash` the tenant hasn't approved**. When a version is dropped, fall back to the next older candidate. An unapproved permission increase therefore holds the tenant on the last approved version; it doesn't break them.
3. **Satisfy service dependencies.** Every required `dependencies.services[]` range must be met by the provider's chosen version.
   - If it isn't, try older candidates of the *consumer*, going back at most 5.
   - If that still fails, mark the plugin `UNRESOLVED` with a reason shown in the admin UI.
   - An unmet `optional` dependency never blocks resolution.
4. **Check for cycles.** Reject any cycle in the service graph; every plugin in it becomes `UNRESOLVED`. The publish step also warns about cycles against the latest versions.
5. **Output.** A `{pluginId → version}` map, one version per plugin per tenant, and the contribution index built from it. The `resolution_id` is recorded on **every report run**, for audit and reproduction.

Resolution is recalculated when catalog, tenant, rollout, or approval data changes, and is cached by input hash.

### 6.4 Contribution index

- The key is `pluginId/contributionId`. Saved reports store this reference together with `plugin_major` and `config_version`.
- The report editor's pickers (data sources, visualizations, and so on) read the index. It never needs a running instance.
- If a contribution's plugin is disabled, unresolved or quarantined, it is **hidden from pickers** but stays resolvable for existing reports, which render it degraded (§7.9).

### 6.5 Desired-state reconciliation

- Instances are **not** started up front. Desired state records only which version *would* run. The router asks for instances on demand; plugins that declare `onStartup` are the exception.
- Each runner's supervisor is the **single writer** for the state of its instances, recorded in `instance_directory`. Host replicas read the directory and send Start, Drain and Stop commands. This avoids split-brain across host replicas.
- If a runner node is lost, its instances become `LOST` after a missed heartbeat window of 15 seconds. The router starts replacements elsewhere, and in-flight invocations fail with retryable `UNAVAILABLE`.

### 6.6 Rollout, rollback, yank, and kill switch

- **Channels.** `canary` covers internal tenants. `stable` rolls out in stages: 1% → 10% → 50% → 100%. The minimum soak per stage defaults to 2h, 12h, 24h and — respectively, and a plugin can lengthen it (never shorten it) in its rollout policy.
- **Automatic rollback triggers** (evaluated per stage, new version against previous, same tenants):
  - activation failure rate above 2%;
  - `INTERNAL`, `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` and crash rate more than 2× the baseline, with at least 200 invocations;
  - any tenant going into crash-loop quarantine.
- **Rollback** sets desired state back to the previous version, and the normal reload flow (§7.5) applies it.
- **Yank** removes a version from resolution. Running instances drain to the next resolvable version.
- **Block** is for security issues. Instances are killed immediately with no drain, and the version can never resolve again.
- **Kill switch.** The platform can disable a plugin for all tenants with one call. Its contributions render as unavailable (§7.9), and reports don't fail as a whole.

## 7. Lifecycle

### 7.1 Instance state machine

```
               start                 handshake ok            activate ok
 (resolved) ---------> STARTING ------------------> LOADED ---------------> ACTIVE <----------+
                           |                          |                     |   |            | health
                           | fail/timeout             | fail/timeout        |   | health x3  | recovers
                           v                          v                     |   v            |
                        FAILED <---------------------------------------------  UNHEALTHY -----+
                           |                                                |   | restart
                           | restart w/ backoff                             |   v
                           |---> STARTING                        drain cmd  |  (FAILED)
                           | 5 crashes / 10 min                             v
                           +---> QUARANTINED                             DRAINING --in-flight done / drain timeout--> DEACTIVATING
                                  (30 min or manual release)                                                            |      |
                                                                                                   deactivate ok  <-----+      +--> timeout -> KILLED
                                                                                                         v
                                                                                                      STOPPED
```

| State | Accepts new invocations | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| STARTING | no (callers wait up to the activation budget) | Process spawned, signature verified, handshake in progress |
| LOADED | no | Handshake done, API version negotiated, `Activate` in progress |
| ACTIVE | **yes** | |
| UNHEALTHY | no (router sends traffic to a sibling or waits for a restart) | 3 health checks missed in a row |
| DRAINING | no; in-flight invocations continue | During reload, idle unload, or runner shutdown |
| DEACTIVATING | no | `Deactivate` hook running |
| STOPPED / KILLED | no | Terminal. `KILLED` is recorded with its cause (timeout, OOM, block) |
| FAILED | no | Retried with backoff |
| QUARANTINED | no | Contributions degraded, owner paged |

Separately, a plugin can be **enabled or disabled per tenant** in the catalog (§6.1). Disabling drains every instance for that tenant.

### 7.2 Hooks

SDK surface (TypeScript shown; the Python SDK mirrors it):

```ts
export default definePlugin({
  // Required. Register every declared contribution here.
  activate(ctx: PluginContext): Promise<void>;

  // Optional. Best-effort cleanup. NOT called after a crash, OOM, or kill.
  deactivate?(reason: DeactivateReason): Promise<void>;

  // Optional. Hand in-memory state to the next instance on a same-major reload.
  exportState?(): Promise<Uint8Array | undefined>;

  // Optional. Only called if manifest lifecycle.supportsLiveConfig = true.
  onConfigChanged?(change: ConfigChange): Promise<"applied" | "restart">;

  // Optional. Required once any contribution has configVersion > 1.
  migrateConfig?(input: MigrateConfigInput): Promise<MigrateConfigResult>;

  // Optional. The SDK default reports SERVING while the event loop is responsive.
  health?(): Promise<HealthStatus>;
});
```

**Two contexts.** Plugins see two kinds of context:

- `PluginContext`, per instance, is passed to `activate`. It provides contribution registration, `logger`, `kv`, `secrets`, `http`, `pluginConfig`, `reload` (`{fromVersion, previousState}`), and `host.supports(feature)`. Its token is an **instance token**: principal `SYSTEM`, with **no data scopes**. Background work, such as refreshing a cache on a timer, uses this context.
- `InvocationContext`, per call, is passed to every contribution method. It provides `tenantId`, `principal`, `deadline`, `signal` (cancellation), `locale`, `timeZone`, and `data`, `http`, `secrets`, `kv`, `logger`, all bound to the **invocation token**.

Registration calls such as `ctx.dataSources.register(id, impl)` return a `Disposable`. The SDK disposes everything registered through `ctx` when the instance deactivates, so a plugin can't leak registrations across a reload.

| Hook | When | Timeout (default / max) | On timeout or error | Guarantees |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Handshake (inside the SDK) | Process start | 5 s | FAILED | — |
| `activate` | First matching activation event, or at start for `onStartup` | 30 s / 120 s | FAILED, process killed, backoff restart | Called exactly once per instance. No invocation arrives before it resolves. Fails if the registered contributions don't match the manifest. |
| `deactivate` | After drain, idle unload, disable, or host shutdown | 10 s / 30 s | SIGTERM, then SIGKILL 5 s later | Called **at most once**. Never rely on it for durability. |
| `exportState` | Reload to a new version with the same major and the same `stateSchemaVersion` | 5 s, ≤ 16 MiB | Ignored; the new instance starts cold | Best-effort. The snapshot is taken while the old instance is still serving, so it may be slightly stale. |
| `onConfigChanged` | Tenant admin changes plugin config | 10 s | Treated as `"restart"` | If not implemented or `supportsLiveConfig` is false, a blue/green restart on the same version |
| `migrateConfig` | Host loads a saved contribution config with an older `configVersion` | 5 s | Contribution degraded; original config kept | Must be **pure and deterministic**. The output is validated against the current schema before it's saved. |
| `health` | Every 15 s | 2 s | 3 misses → UNHEALTHY → restart | — |

**Cancellation.** Every invocation has a deadline and a cancellation signal (gRPC cancel, surfaced as `inv.signal` or `inv.cancelled`). After the deadline the host waits a 2-second grace period, then reports `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`. An instance that ignores cancellation more than 10 times in a minute is recycled.

**Secrets and rotation.** Secrets are fetched on demand and cached by the SDK for at most 60 seconds, so rotating a secret needs no reload.

### 7.3 Activation events

| Event | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `onContribution:<id>` | Any invocation of that contribution. **This is the default**: if `activation` is omitted, every contribution is included. |
| `onEvent:<eventType>` | Delivery of that event to an action contribution |
| `onService:<serviceId>` | A brokered call to that service |
| `onStartup` | Start as soon as the version resolves for a tenant. Discouraged, and requires platform approval in review. |

- **Cold-start budget.** p95 of handshake plus activation must be under 3 seconds; conformance measures it.
- **Warm pool.** The supervisor keeps `minWarm` instances ready, based on the previous hour's invocation rate for each (plugin, tenant).
- **Idle unload.** An instance with no invocations for `idleTimeoutSec` (default 900, range 60–3600) drains gracefully.

### 7.4 Invocation flow

1. The report engine asks the router for `contributionRef` in tenant T.
2. The router looks up the version in the contribution index, then finds an ACTIVE instance or requests a start. Concurrent requests for the same instance share a single start.
3. The router checks the circuit breaker and `maxConcurrency`. Excess calls queue up to `2 × maxConcurrency`; beyond that they fail with `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`.
4. The router validates contribution config against `configSchema`, running `migrateConfig` first if needed.
5. The router mints an **invocation token**. It is opaque and bound to the instance, tenant, principal, contribution and the plugin's approved permissions, and it expires at deadline + 30 s.
6. The router calls the plugin RPC with `InvocationContext`.
7. The plugin makes `HostServices` calls with the token, and the broker authorizes each one (§8.3).
8. The host validates the output (schema, size caps, sanitization per §8.7) as it streams. When the call ends, the token is revoked.

### 7.5 Reload: upgrade, rollback, or restart on the same version

Reload is **blue/green per instance** and never reduces availability.

1. Desired state becomes V2. The registry starts a V2 instance, which moves through STARTING and LOADED.
2. If V1 is ACTIVE, V2 has the same plugin major, and `stateSchemaVersion` matches, the registry calls `ExportState` on V1 (which keeps serving) and passes the snapshot to V2 as `ctx.reload.previousState`.
3. When V2 is ACTIVE, the router **switches new invocations to V2 atomically**.
4. V1 enters DRAINING. In-flight work may run for up to `drainTimeoutSec` (default 60, max 900 for long exports).
5. After that, remaining V1 invocations are cancelled with `UNAVAILABLE`, reason `PLUGIN_RELOADING`. The host retries the call once on V2 **only if the plugin hasn't yet emitted output to the report engine** and the kind is retry-safe (`dataSource`, `transform`, `visualization`, `exporter`). Otherwise the error goes to the run-level retry policy. Actions are always redelivered through the event queue.
6. The registry calls `Deactivate` on V1, which then moves to STOPPED.

**If V2 fails** handshake or activation, V1 stays ACTIVE, the version is marked failed for this tenant, and the §6.6 rollback policy is evaluated.

**Invariants**

- At most **two** instances exist per (plugin, tenant), and at most one of them is draining.
- **Mixed-version window:** during a drain, V1 and V2 both run. The KV namespace is per (plugin, tenant) and **shared across versions**, so stored data must stay readable in both directions for adjacent versions. Across a major version there is no state handoff; V2 migrates KV records lazily, using version-tagged records.

### 7.6 Other reload triggers

| Trigger | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Crash, OOM, or CPU-limit kill | The supervisor restarts the same version with exponential backoff from 1 s, capped at 60 s. **5 crashes in 10 minutes** → QUARANTINED for 30 minutes, `owner.oncall` is paged, and contributions are degraded. Platform or owner can release it early with `rpt-plugin quarantine release`. |
| Plugin config change | `onConfigChanged`, or a blue/green restart on the same version |
| Permission approval or version pin change | Resolution runs again, followed by the normal reload |
| Runner node drain or host upgrade | Instances drain and restart on other nodes. `deactivate(reason: HOST_SHUTDOWN)` is called. |
| `rpt-plugin dev` file change | Blue/green with drain timeout 0 |

### 7.7 Config migration for saved reports

- Each contribution has an integer `configVersion`. A plugin must migrate from **every `configVersion` shipped in its current and previous major**. Conformance enforces this with fixtures at `test/fixtures/config/<contributionId>/<n>.json`.
- The host migrates **lazily**, when a report is opened or run. It validates the result, writes it back, and keeps the pre-migration copy for 90 days.
- **Rolling back** to a plugin version with a lower `configVersion` works like this:
  - If the report hasn't been edited since migration, the host restores the saved pre-migration copy.
  - Otherwise the contribution renders degraded with "requires plugin ≥ X.Y".
- On a plugin major bump, `contribution_usage` shows the blast radius before publish, and the CLI prints the number of affected reports per tenant.

### 7.8 Dependencies and ordering

- Plugins never hold connections to each other, so **start and stop need no ordering**. A provider activates lazily when its service is first called (`onService:`).
- When a provider is upgraded within its range, consumers are **not** restarted.
- If a provider becomes unresolved, quarantined, or disabled:
  - a consumer with a **required** dependency sees its contributions become DEGRADED;
  - with an **optional** dependency, calls return `UNAVAILABLE` with reason `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, and the plugin handles it.

### 7.9 Degraded rendering

If a contribution fails, the rest of the report still renders. The failed block is replaced by a placeholder showing the plugin name, the error's `user_message`, and a correlation ID. A report or schedule can set `strict: true`, for example for regulated deliveries; then any contribution failure fails the whole run and nothing partial is sent.

## 8. Sandbox and security

### 8.1 Threat model

**Assets:** tenant report data, tenant secrets, host availability, and isolation between tenants.

| ID | Threat | Primary control |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | A buggy plugin crashes, hangs, leaks, spins the CPU, or produces huge output | Process isolation, cgroups, deadlines, output caps |
| T2 | A compromised dependency inside a plugin tries to exfiltrate data or secrets | No ambient network; broker-only egress to allowlisted hosts; secret refs |
| T3 | A plugin reads data the invoking user can't access (confused deputy) | Effective scopes = manifest ∩ tenant approval ∩ principal's permissions |
| T4 | Data leaks across tenants through shared memory or caches | One process per (plugin, version, tenant) |
| T5 | A sandbox escape reaches the runner node | gVisor, seccomp, no credentials on the node, dedicated node pool |
| T6 | A malicious client visualization attacks a user's session | Sandboxed cross-origin iframe, strict CSP, no network |
| T7 | A supply-chain attack on the bundle in transit or at rest | Signatures verified at publish **and** at every start |

**Out of scope:** malicious platform operators, and hardware side channels across VM boundaries.

### 8.2 Isolation design

**Rejected alternatives**

- **In-process loading** (`import` or `require`): no memory or CPU isolation, and full ambient authority.
- **Node `vm` or realms:** Node's own documentation says they are not a security mechanism.
- **V8 isolates (`isolated-vm`):** they work only for JavaScript (no Python), and a native bug crashes the whole shared process.
- **WASM (component model / WASI 0.2):** it has the best capability model, but team libraries (database drivers, PDF engines) don't run well on it yet. The manifest reserves `runtime.type: "wasm"` for a later tier behind the **same proto contract**.

**Chosen design:** one OS process per (plugin, version, tenant), inside a gVisor-sandboxed container on dedicated runner nodes. The isolation layers:

| # | Layer | Mechanism | Stops |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Capability broker** | All I/O goes through `HostServices`, and each call is authorized by its token. **Behaves the same in dev and prod.** | T2, T3 |
| 2 | Process and tenant separation | One process per (plugin, version, tenant); no shared memory or filesystem | T1, T4 |
| 3 | Kernel sandbox | gVisor (`runsc`), seccomp default-deny, non-root UID, all Linux capabilities dropped, read-only rootfs, bundle mounted read-only, `/tmp` as a size-capped tmpfs | T5 |
| 4 | Network | Network namespace with **no interfaces except loopback**. The only way out is two Unix sockets to the supervisor proxy: one for the plugin's gRPC server, one for `HostServices`. | T2 |
| 5 | Resources | cgroups v2 limits on memory, CPU quota, pids (≤ 64) and open files (≤ 1024) | T1 |
| 6 | Node | Dedicated tainted node pool, IMDS blocked, no service-account token mounted, sandboxes can't reach the cluster network | T5 |
| 7 | Browser | Client bundles load from a separate origin (`plugins-content.<domain>`) in `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts">`, so the origin is opaque. CSP is `default-src 'none'; script-src <bundle-origin>; style-src <bundle-origin> 'unsafe-inline'; img-src blob: data:`. Communication uses postMessage only, and the host validates every message against the protocol schema. | T6 |

The sandbox environment contains no variables except `RPT_PLUGIN_SOCKET`, `RPT_HOST_SOCKET` and `RPT_INSTANCE_ID`, and no credentials.

**Local development** (`rpt-plugin dev` on Windows, macOS or Linux) uses plain process isolation, so layers 3–6 are missing and the dev UI shows a banner saying so. Layer 1 is still enforced, so **permission mistakes show up locally**, not first in production.

### 8.3 Capability broker and permissions

**Effective access for a `HostServices` call** = manifest permission ∩ tenant-approved permissions hash ∩ (for data scopes) the RBAC of the token's principal.

| Permission | Manifest form | Unlocks | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `network` | `[{host, ports?, methods?}]`. `host` is an exact name or a single-label wildcard (`*.api.example.com`). IP literals aren't allowed. | `HttpFetch` | The broker resolves DNS itself and rejects private, loopback, link-local and metadata addresses (**SSRF**). It pins the resolved IP for the connection, requires TLS 1.2+ (HTTP only for `ports: [80]` when explicitly declared), caps responses at 50 MiB by default, allows at most 100 requests per invocation by default, and doesn't follow redirects to hosts outside the allowlist. |
| `secrets` | `[{name, description}]` | `GetSecret(name)`, and `secret_ref` header substitution in `HttpFetch` | Tenant admins store the values in the host vault. Only declared names can be read. **Prefer `secret_ref`**: the broker inserts the value into the outgoing request and the plugin never holds it. Values are removed from logs by both the SDK and the broker. |
| `data` | Scopes: `datasets:read`, `datasets:write`, `reports:read`, `directory:read-basic` | `QueryDataset`, `GetArtifact`, principal display names | Always intersected with the invoking principal's RBAC. **Instance tokens (`SYSTEM`) never have data scopes.** Scheduled runs use the schedule owner as principal. |
| `storage` | `{kvQuotaMiB}` (1–1024) | `Kv*` | Namespace per (plugin, tenant), shared across versions. Values ≤ 1 MiB, keys ≤ 512 bytes, optional TTL, compare-and-set by revision. No plugin can read another's namespace. |
| (dependencies) | `dependencies.services[]` | `InvokeService` | The callee runs under the **caller's invocation principal**. Its effective access is the callee's permissions ∩ that principal, never more. |

**Always allowed:** `Log`, `EmitMetrics`, and reading the plugin's own config (delivered in `Activate` and `ConfigChanged`).

**Approval.** When enabling a plugin, a tenant admin sees a plain-language list of its permissions. On upgrade they see only the **diff**. For first-party plugins in managed tenants, the platform may pre-approve for the whole org (open question Q6), and those approvals are still recorded in `permission_approval`.

**Audit.** Every broker call is written to the tenant-visible audit log: timestamp, plugin, version, tenant, principal, capability, target (host, secret name, dataset, service), outcome and bytes.

### 8.4 Resource limits

| Resource | Default | Max without approval | Hard max |
|---|---|---|---|
| `memoryMiB` | 256 | 1024 | 4096 |
| `cpuMillis` (quota) | 500 | 2000 | 4000 |
| `invocationTimeoutMs` | 30 000 | 300 000 | 1 800 000 |
| `maxConcurrency` (per instance) | 4 | 32 | 64 |
| `maxOutputMiB` (per invocation, streamed) | 256 | 1024 | 4096 |
| `tmpDiskMiB` | 256 | 1024 | 4096 |
| `lifecycle.activateTimeoutMs` | 30 000 | 120 000 | 120 000 |
| `HttpFetch` requests per invocation | 100 | 1000 | 10 000 |

**Tenant fair use.** Each tenant has a budget of plugin CPU-seconds per hour, summed across its instances. Going over it **throttles**: invocations queue with lower priority. They don't fail.

### 8.5 Tenant isolation cost

Per-tenant instances multiply process count. Three things keep this manageable: lazy activation, idle unload, a small default memory size, and a warm pool only where there is traffic.

v1 has **no "shared across tenants" mode**. Even a pure-render plugin holds tenant data in memory, and a compromised one could leak it into another tenant's output. If the active instance count grows past what runners can handle (open question Q2), the fix is the WASM tier, where creating a fresh instance per invocation is cheap. Relaxing isolation is not the fix.

### 8.6 Supply chain

- Signed bundles use keyless Sigstore signing with identity bound to the team's CI. Signatures are verified at publish and at every sandbox start.
- A lockfile is required, and dependencies are vendored into the bundle. **Nothing is installed at runtime**, and the sandbox has no network to install from anyway.
- The SBOM is scanned at publish and **rescanned nightly** for every published version. New critical findings notify the owner. Critical findings that are actively exploited can be blocked by the platform (§6.6).
- Native add-ons are allowed only if built in the SDK's official build image, for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64.

### 8.7 Plugin output is untrusted

- Arrow streams are validated against the declared or resolved schema.
- SVG is sanitized before it's embedded anywhere: scripts, event-handler attributes, `foreignObject` and external references are stripped.
- `html_static` output is only ever displayed inside the layer-7 sandboxed iframe.
- Exporter MIME types must match the manifest, and file names are sanitized.
- Error `user_message` values are shown as plain text, never HTML, and capped at 500 characters.

## 9. Versioned API contract

### 9.1 What "the API" includes

1. **Wire protocol:** proto package `reporting.plugin.v1` (`proto/reporting/plugin/v1/`). This is **normative**.
2. **Semantics:** the lifecycle guarantees, timeouts, retry rules, and error handling in this document.
3. **Data conventions:** Arrow usage, the `Expression` function set, event payload schemas, and the report document model.
4. **Manifest schema:** versioned separately through `manifestVersion`.
5. **Browser protocol:** `client-viz/1`.
6. **SDKs:** `@reporting/plugin-sdk` (npm) and `reporting-plugin-sdk` (PyPI). **SDKs have their own semver.** Each SDK release declares which API versions it supports.

### 9.2 Version identifiers

- The host API version is `MAJOR.MINOR`, e.g. `1.4`. It has no patch number, because host bug fixes don't change the contract.
- The proto package carries only the major (`v1`, `v2`). Minors are additive changes inside the package.
- Plugins declare caret ranges in `api.version`. `"^1.4 || ^2.0"` lets one bundle run on both v1 and v2 hosts during a migration.

### 9.3 Handshake and feature negotiation

1. The host calls `PluginRuntime.Handshake` with the highest minor it supports for each major (e.g. `[1.6, 2.1]`) and its list of **feature flags**.
2. The SDK picks the **highest version** in the intersection of the host's offer, the SDK's own support, and the manifest's `api.version`, then returns it along with the proto services it implements.
3. The host checks that the selection falls inside the manifest range, then speaks exactly that version to the instance through its adapter layer (§9.5).
4. If there's no overlap, the instance fails with `API_INCOMPATIBLE`. Resolution should have prevented this; the handshake is the backstop.

Every minor-level addition has a **named feature** (e.g. `dataSource.sampling`, `hostServices.kvList`) listed in `API_CHANGELOG.md` with the minor that introduced it.

- A plugin that **requires** a feature raises its minimum `api.version`.
- A plugin that uses a feature **optionally** checks `ctx.host.supports("…")`.

### 9.4 Compatibility rules

**Allowed in a minor release:**

- adding RPCs, messages, optional fields, enum values, `HostServices` methods, extension-point capabilities, event types, or error reasons;
- relaxing a limit;
- adding a `Expression` function (plugins don't push down functions they don't know).

**Plugins must** (the SDK enforces this and conformance fuzzes for it):

- ignore unknown fields;
- map unknown enum values to the documented fallback (usually `*_UNSPECIFIED`, handled conservatively);
- ignore unknown event types, which is a successful no-op;
- never depend on error message text or field order.

**The host must:**

- never send an instance anything newer than its negotiated version (the adapter removes or converts it);
- apply the documented default for an optional plugin RPC the plugin doesn't implement. For example, a missing `MigrateConfig` means "config at version 1 only", and a missing `ExportState` means a cold start.

**Breaking changes (major only):**

- removing or renaming fields, RPCs or enum values;
- changing field types or semantics;
- tightening validation;
- changing default behavior;
- lowering a documented timeout or limit;
- changing lifecycle ordering or guarantees.

**Tooling:**

- `buf breaking --against <last release tag>` is required in CI for the proto repository.
- PRs that change semantics without touching the proto need the `api-review` label and sign-off (§13).
- Manifest schema changes follow the same rules under `manifestVersion`.

### 9.5 Support policy

- The host supports the **current major N and the previous major N−1**.
- N−1 stays supported for **at least 6 months after N reaches GA**. Its sunset date is announced **at least one full quarter before** it takes effect.
- Every minor within a supported major stays supported, which follows from minors being additive.
- Inside the host, each wire major is served by an **adapter** that translates between `vN` messages and the host's internal model. The internal model is never exposed on the wire, which keeps N−1 support cheap and contained.
- **Preview APIs:** preview RPCs live in `reporting.plugin.v1preview`, and preview features are flagged `proposed`. To use one, a plugin must list it in `api.proposed`. Such versions can only publish to `canary`. Preview APIs may change without notice and graduate into a minor release.

### 9.6 Deprecation

- Deprecated items are marked `[deprecated = true]` in the proto, with a comment giving `sunset: YYYY-MM-DD` and the replacement.
- The broker and router emit `plugin_api_deprecated_usage_total{plugin, version, feature}`. Owning teams get a weekly digest, and `rpt-plugin validate` and publish show warnings.
- Deprecated items are removed only in a new major.

### 9.7 Contract testing

- **Conformance kit** (`@reporting/plugin-conformance`, also a CLI command) runs a bundle against a reference host at every API version it claims. It checks:
  - handshake and version selection;
  - activation and cold-start budgets;
  - that registered contributions match the manifest;
  - that cancellation is honored;
  - that `deactivate` finishes on time;
  - **tolerance of unknown fields and enum values** (by fuzzing);
  - that each contribution's contract holds for the plugin's fixtures (`test/fixtures/<kind>/<id>/…`);
  - config migration for every published `configVersion`;
  - that service schemas are honored.
- **Consumer-driven host CI:** every host release candidate runs the conformance kit against the **latest published version of every plugin** in the catalog, plus the version currently on `stable`. A host change that breaks a published plugin blocks the release. This check is what actually makes "a minor never breaks you" true.
- Plugin CI runs the kit on every PR, at the minimum and maximum API version the plugin claims.

### 9.8 A plugin's own public contract

Other people depend on a plugin's contribution IDs, config schemas, service schemas, and supported `configVersion` values. §5.2.9 lists what forces a plugin major bump, and the publish diff checker enforces every rule it can check mechanically.

### 9.9 Change log

`API_CHANGELOG.md` has one entry per minor: new features and their flags, deprecations with sunset dates, the minimum SDK version, and the adapter's behavior for older minors.

## 10. Error model

Errors use a **gRPC status code** plus a `PluginError` detail message (`common.proto`), in both directions.

```
PluginError { reason, retryable, retry_after, user_message, debug_message, field_violations[] }
```

- **`reason`** is UPPER_SNAKE. Host-defined reasons are bare (`CAPABILITY_NOT_DECLARED`). Plugin-defined reasons are namespaced (`com.example.finance.ledger-connector/RATE_LIMITED`).
- **`user_message`** is shown to end users, so it must be safe and must not contain secrets.
- **`debug_message`** goes to logs only.
- **`field_violations`** use JSON Pointer paths into the config, so the editor can highlight the fields.

| Code | Typical cause | Host behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `INVALID_ARGUMENT` | Bad config or parameters | No retry. Highlight fields in the editor. |
| `FAILED_PRECONDITION` | Upstream credential expired, dataset deleted | No retry. Prompt the admin or author. |
| `PERMISSION_DENIED` | Upstream or broker denied access | No retry. The broker uses reason `CAPABILITY_NOT_DECLARED` (fix the manifest) or `PRINCIPAL_LACKS_ACCESS` (the user's RBAC), so developers can tell them apart. |
| `NOT_FOUND` | Dataset or object missing | No retry |
| `UNAVAILABLE` | Upstream down, plugin reloading, crash mid-call | Retry ≤ 3 with backoff within the deadline, subject to the no-output-yet rule in §7.5 |
| `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` | Rate limit, quota, concurrency | Retry after `retry_after` if it fits within the deadline |
| `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` | Too slow | Interactive: no retry. Scheduled: one retry. |
| `INTERNAL` / `UNKNOWN` | Bug | No retry. Counts toward the rollout error guard (§6.6). |

## 11. Observability

- **Logs.** The SDK logger sends batches to `HostServices.Log`.
  - Every line is tagged automatically with `plugin`, `version`, `tenant`, `instance`, `invocation` and `trace_id`.
  - stdout and stderr are captured as a fallback at level `warn`.
  - Limits: 1000 lines per minute per instance, 16 KiB per line. Secrets are removed.
  - Retention is 14 days. Owning teams can read their plugin's logs, and that access is audited.
- **Host-side metrics** need nothing from the plugin: invocations, latency histograms, errors by code and reason, activation time, crashes by cause, memory and CPU, drain duration, queue depth, broker calls by capability, and deprecated-API usage.
- **Custom plugin metrics** go through `EmitMetrics`. Names are prefixed `plugin_<sanitized id>_`, capped at 1000 series per plugin, and label names are validated.
- **Tracing.** W3C `traceparent` travels in `InvocationContext`. The SDK creates spans automatically for contribution methods and host calls, and `HttpFetch` passes trace context to upstream services.
- **Provisioned on first publish, from `owner`:** a per-plugin dashboard and alerts (crash loop, error rate, p95 latency, quarantine). Cross-tenant dashboards show aggregates only.

## 13. Governance

- **Namespaces.** `com.example.<team>.*` maps to a team in the catalog, bound to that team's CI signing identity.
- **The platform team owns** the host, proto, adapters, SDKs, catalog, runners, conformance kit, CLI, and this document.
- **Plugin teams own** their plugins, conformance fixtures, on-call for their plugins (quarantine pages go to them), and data and permission justification during review.
- **Changing the API or adding an extension point:**
  1. an RFC PR against this document and the proto;
  2. API review by the platform team plus at least 2 plugin teams;
  3. release in `v1preview`;
  4. at least one plugin uses it on `canary`;
  5. GA in the next minor.
- **During the build quarter:** a weekly sync with plugin teams, a shared channel, and a platform response to API blockers within **2 business days**.

---

## 14. Delivery plan

The key point for the timeline: **all enforcement happens on the host side** (the broker, router and supervisor), so plugin code has no dependency on sandbox hardening or rollout machinery. What teams need on day 1 is a **frozen contract, an SDK, and `rpt-plugin dev`**. Everything else can ship in parallel without changing plugin code.

If "next quarter" starts on 2026-10-01, that leaves about 2 weeks, so Phase 0 is the critical path.

| Phase | Scope | Exit criteria |
|---|---|---|
| **0: Freeze** (now → quarter start) | Review this doc; confirm assumptions A1–A5; each of the 5 teams lists its first plugins and their kinds, permissions and data scopes. Close any extension-point gaps. Freeze manifest v1 and proto `v1` as **1.0-rc**. | Signed-off doc; 1.0-rc tagged; every team's first plugin fits the extension points |
| **1: Build against it** (weeks 1–4) | TypeScript SDK; `rpt-plugin init/validate/dev/test`; local host with broker (every permission), router, lifecycle hooks, reload; conformance kit v0 | Every team has a plugin running in `dev` and passing conformance v0 |
| **2: Ship to canary** (weeks 4–8) | Catalog and publish pipeline (signing, checks); runners with process isolation and cgroups; blue/green reload; canary channel; config migration; Python SDK; client-viz iframe | Every team publishes to canary; internal tenants use real reports |
| **3: Harden and GA** (weeks 8–12) | gVisor, network namespaces and node pool; staged rollout with auto-rollback; dashboards and alerts; consumer-driven host CI; external security review and pen test of the sandbox and broker; **API 1.0 GA** | Pen test findings closed; first plugins on `stable` |

**Changes allowed to 1.0-rc before GA:** additive changes only, plus fixes to real defects agreed in API review. Plugin teams are told about every change 48 hours before it merges.

```ts
import { definePlugin, arrow, PluginError, Code } from "@reporting/plugin-sdk";

let fxCache: Map<string, number> = new Map();

export default definePlugin({
  async activate(ctx) {
    if (ctx.reload?.previousState) fxCache = decodeCache(ctx.reload.previousState);

    ctx.dataSources.register("ledger", {
      async testConnection({ config }, inv) {
        const res = await inv.http.fetch(`https://${config.region}.api.ledger.example.com/v2/ping`, {
          headers: { Authorization: { secretRef: "ledger.apiKey" } }, // broker injects the value
          signal: inv.signal,
        });
        return res.ok ? { ok: true } : { ok: false, userMessage: `Ledger returned ${res.status}` };
      },

      async describe({ config }, inv) {
        return { datasets: [{ name: "journal_entries", schema: JOURNAL_SCHEMA, supportsIncremental: true }] };
      },

      async *query(req, inv) {
        const pushed = req.filters.filter((f) => canPushDown(f.expr));
        let cursor = req.cursor;
        do {
          const page = await fetchPage(inv, req.config, pushed, cursor);
```
