```
  ┌──────────────────────────── Host (reporting service, N replicas) ─────────────────────────────┐
  │                                                                                                 │
  │  Report engine ──▶ Extension Point Router ──▶ Plugin Supervisor ──▶ Instance Pool (per plugin@v, │
  │       ▲                   │                       │  (lifecycle FSM,     per tenant if needed)  │
  │       │                   │                       │   reconciler,              │               │
  │  Output validators ◀──────┘                       │   health, breaker)         │               │
  │                                                   ▼                            │ RPC channel   │
  │                                           Capability Broker ◀──────────────────┤ (UDS/pipe)    │
  │                                     (fetch, data.query, kv, secrets,           │               │
  │                                      services, log, metrics; policy checks)    │               │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────┘
                                                                                   │
                                        ┌──────────── Sandbox (one per instance) ──┴──────────────┐
                                        │ gVisor/nsjail container: no netns, RO rootfs, cgroups   │
                                        │  └─ node --permission … plugin-runtime (SDK)            │
                                        │       └─ plugin bundle (dist/index.js)                  │
                                        └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Components

| Component | Responsibility | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| **Registry API** | Publishers, plugins, releases, installations, grants; the source of truth | Platform |
| **Verification pipeline** | Gates a release before it can be installed (§4.3) | Platform |
| **Artifact store** | Immutable, content-addressed package blobs | Platform |
| **Resolver** | Turns installations into a deterministic *Resolved Plan* per environment | Platform |
| **Plugin Supervisor** | Lifecycle state machine, reconciliation, restarts, circuit breaking, drain | Platform |
| **Instance Pool** | Scales sandboxed instances within manifest limits and routes invocations | Platform |
| **Extension Point Router** | Maps a contribution reference in a report to a pool and handles version and param migration | Platform |
| **Capability Broker** | The only path from a plugin to the outside world; enforces permissions | Platform |
| **Output validators** | Treat every plugin output as untrusted (schema, size, sanitization) | Platform |
| **plugin-runtime** | In-sandbox shim: protocol, handshake, dispatch, SDK bindings | Platform (ships in SDK) |
| **Plugins** | Contributions to extension points | The five teams |

The principle behind the layout is **control plane / data plane separation**. The registry can be down and hosts keep running their last applied Resolved Plan. Hosts never call the registry on the invocation path.

## 3. Extension points (v1)

Every contribution is addressed by a **fully qualified contribution ID (FQCID)**:

```
<pluginId>:<contributionId>          e.g. @finance/netsuite-connector:netsuite
```

Because plugin IDs are namespaced by team (§4.1), contributions cannot collide.

| Extension point | What it does | Input → Output | Default deadline |
|---|---|---|---|
| `datasource` | Connects to an external system, discovers schema, runs queries | config + query → Arrow stream | 300 s |
| `transform` | Reshapes tabular data | params + N Arrow streams → Arrow stream | 120 s |
| `visualization` | Renders a chart or widget | spec + Arrow table → Vega-Lite spec **or** sanitized SVG | 30 s |
| `exporter` | Produces a file from a rendered report | report document + options → blob (PDF, XLSX, CSV…) | 180 s |
| `delivery` | Sends artifacts somewhere | artifacts + target → delivery receipt | 60 s |

The set of extension points is itself part of the versioned API. A new extension point is a minor API bump (§7).

### 3.1 Datasource
Methods: `testConnection`, `discoverSchema`, `query`, and optionally `estimate`.
It advertises **pushdown capabilities** (`filter`, `project`, `limit`, `sort`, `aggregate`). The report engine pushes down what it can and executes the rest in the host.
`query` returns a stream, and the host applies backpressure (§7.6).

### 3.2 Transform
Methods: `validateParams`, `outputSchema`, `execute`.
`outputSchema` must be **pure and fast** (≤ 2 s). The report editor calls it on every edit to show columns without executing anything.
The host checks that the batches `execute` produces match the schema `outputSchema` returned.

### 3.3 Visualization
Methods: `validateSpec`, `dataRequirements`, `render`.
**Decision:** v1 visualizations return declarative output only. That means a Vega-Lite spec, which the host's trusted client renderer draws, or SVG, which the host sanitizes with an allowlist of elements and attributes: no `<script>`, no `<foreignObject>`, no event handlers, and no external `href`.
This avoids running plugin code in the browser, and with it the need for a second sandbox (iframe, CSP, postMessage bridge). If teams need interactive custom widgets, that becomes the v2 "client extension point" with its own design.

### 3.4 Exporter
Methods: `export`.
The manifest declares output MIME types. The host checks magic bytes against the declared type and enforces `limits.maxOutputBytes`.

### 3.5 Delivery
Methods: `validateTarget`, `deliver`.
Every `deliver` call carries an `idempotencyKey`, and plugins **must** treat a repeated key as a no-op returning the original receipt. Scheduled deliveries are retried on `retryable` errors, so this is required.

### 3.6 Saved-report compatibility (critical for a reporting tool)
Saved reports store `{ fqcid, pluginMajor, paramsSchemaVersion, params }`.
- Each contribution declares `paramsSchemaVersion` (an integer) in the manifest.
- When a plugin raises `paramsSchemaVersion`, it **must** implement `migrateParams(fromVersion, params)`. The router calls it lazily on load and the report engine writes the result back.
- If a report references a plugin that is not installed, disabled, or revoked, the widget renders a "plugin unavailable" placeholder. **Reports are never deleted or corrupted because a plugin is missing.**
- Pinning a report to `pluginMajor` means a plugin major bump doesn't silently change saved reports. Admins upgrade reports explicitly with a bulk migration tool, which reuses `migrateParams`.

## 4. Plugin registry

### 4.1 Identity and namespaces
- A plugin ID has the form `@<namespace>/<name>`, matching `^@[a-z0-9-]{2,32}/[a-z0-9-]{2,64}$`.
- The platform team maps a **namespace to an owning team** (one or more namespaces per team). Only keys registered to that team can publish under the namespace.
- The `@platform/` namespace is reserved.

### 4.2 Data model

```
Publisher     (namespace PK, team, contacts[], signingKeys[] {keyId, publicKey, status, notAfter})
Plugin        (id PK, namespace FK, displayName, createdAt, archived)
Release       (pluginId, version) PK
              digest sha256, manifest jsonb, signature, provenanceAttestation, sbom,
              status: pending | verifying | rejected | published | yanked | revoked,
              channel: dev | beta | stable,
              permissionDiff jsonb (vs previous published release),
              verification report jsonb, publishedAt
Environment   (id PK, name: dev | staging | prod-<region>, hostApiRange)
Installation  (id PK, environmentId, pluginId, scope: global | tenant:<id>,
              versionConstraint (semver range) | pinnedVersion, channel,
              enabled bool, configRef → config store, grantId FK)
Grant         (id PK, installationId, permissions jsonb (subset of manifest request),
              approvedBy, approvedAt, releaseDigestApproved)
ResolvedPlan  (environmentId, generation bigint PK, entries[] {pluginId, version, digest,
              scopes[], grantId}, createdAt, cause)
AuditEvent    (append-only; every mutation above + every revoke/quarantine)
```

### 4.3 Publish pipeline

```
rplug pack  →  rplug sign  →  rplug publish  →  [registry] ────────────────────────────┐
                                                 1. Upload to CAS (digest = sha256)      │
                                                 2. Manifest schema validation           │
                                                 3. Signature verifies against namespace │
                                                    publisher key; key not expired       │
                                                 4. Version is new & > all published     │
                                                    (immutable; no overwrite ever)       │
                                                 5. Package lint: no native addons,      │
                                                    size ≤ 50 MB, main exists,           │
                                                    contributions declared == exported   │
                                                 6. SBOM present; dependency vuln scan   │
                                                    (block on critical)                  │
                                                 7. Provenance: built by CI (SLSA L2+    │
                                                    attestation) — required for stable   │
                                                 8. Conformance suite in real sandbox    │
                                                    (§9.3) against every host API minor  │
                                                    in the declared engines range         │
                                                 9. Compute permissionDiff vs previous   │
                                                 ─────────────────────────────────────── │
                                                 status = published | rejected (report) ◀┘
```

- **Channels.** `dev` skips step 7 and can only be installed in dev environments. `beta` can be installed in staging and in prod for allowlisted tenants. `stable` can go anywhere.
- **Promotion** (dev → beta → stable) re-runs nothing. It is a metadata change on the same digest, so what was tested is exactly what ships.

### 4.4 Installation and grants
- Installing a plugin creates an Installation and a Grant. The admin sees the manifest's requested permissions and can **grant a subset**. Anything not granted is denied at runtime.
- If the plugin can't work without a permission, it should mark that permission `required: true` in the manifest. Installation then fails unless it's granted, instead of the plugin failing later at runtime.
- **Permission escalation on upgrade.** If a new release's `permissionDiff` adds permissions or widens scopes, auto-upgrade stops at the previous version and an approval request goes to the installation's admins. A release that *reduces* permissions upgrades automatically.
- Config lives in the host's config store, and secrets live in the vault. Neither goes in the registry. The Installation only holds references.

### 4.5 Resolution
The resolver runs whenever an installation, release status, or environment changes.

1. For each enabled installation, take candidate releases that satisfy all of these:
   - the version constraint or pin
   - the channel is allowed in this environment
   - status is `published` (yanked releases stay allowed only if already resolved)
   - `engines.pluginApi` intersects the environment's `hostApiRange`
   - the grant covers the release's `required` permissions
2. Resolve `dependencies` (§4.6) by picking the highest version that satisfies every dependent's range. Multiple majors of the same plugin **may** coexist when dependents require different majors, because each runs as its own process.
3. Reject cycles and unsatisfiable graphs. **Fail closed per plugin**: the affected plugin and its dependents stay on their last good resolution, and everything else still resolves.
4. Emit a new `ResolvedPlan` generation with a human-readable diff against the previous one (`+ @finance/netsuite-connector 2.3.1`, `~ @ops/slack-delivery 1.4.0 → 1.5.0`).

Resolution is deterministic: the same inputs always produce the same plan. The plan is the only thing hosts consume.

### 4.6 Inter-plugin dependencies
- A plugin can declare `provides.services[]`: named RPC interfaces with a JSON Schema for each method.
- Another plugin can declare `dependencies: { "@platform/fx-rates": "^1.0.0" }` and call `inv.services.get("@platform/fx-rates", "rates").call("convert", args)`.
- Calls always go **through the broker**. There is no direct process-to-process channel. The callee runs with the *original invoking principal* and *its own* grant, and the call chain is propagated for tracing and loop detection (max depth 4).
- Load order is topological, unload order is the reverse, and reloading a dependency doesn't restart dependents. Service calls are routed per call, so the swap is transparent.

### 4.7 Yank, revoke, archive
| Action | Effect | Who |
|---|---|---|
| **Yank** | No new resolutions select it. Running instances continue. | Owning team or platform |
| **Revoke** | Kill switch. It is removed from all plans immediately, hosts force-unload within **60 s** (no drain), and dependents go to `DEGRADED`. | Platform or security only; always audited |
| **Archive plugin** | No new releases or installs. Existing installs are untouched. | Owning team |

### 4.8 Registry API (REST, versioned under `/v1`)

```
POST   /v1/publishers/{ns}/keys                    register signing key (platform-approved)
POST   /v1/plugins/{id}/releases                   publish (multipart: package, signature, attestation)
GET    /v1/plugins/{id}/releases/{version}         release + verification report
POST   /v1/plugins/{id}/releases/{version}:promote {channel}
POST   /v1/plugins/{id}/releases/{version}:yank    {reason}
POST   /v1/plugins/{id}/releases/{version}:revoke  {reason, incidentId}
GET    /v1/plugins?namespace=&extensionPoint=&q=   search
POST   /v1/environments/{env}/installations        create (returns permission request to approve)
PATCH  /v1/environments/{env}/installations/{id}   enable/disable, constraint, channel
POST   /v1/environments/{env}/installations/{id}/grants   approve permissions
GET    /v1/environments/{env}/plan                 current ResolvedPlan (ETag = generation)
GET    /v1/environments/{env}/plan:watch           long-poll / SSE for new generations
GET    /v1/audit?pluginId=&since=
```

Hosts cache the last plan and all referenced artifacts on local disk, verifying each digest on read. That lets them cold-start while the registry is unavailable.

## 5. Lifecycle

### 5.1 State machine (per plugin instance pool, keyed by `pluginId@version[/tenant]`)

```
               plan adds
  (absent) ─────────────▶ PENDING ──fetch+verify digest──▶ RESOLVED
                             │ fail                            │ activation event / minInstances>0
                             ▼                                 ▼
                          FAILED ◀────activate timeout/err── STARTING
                             ▲                                 │ activate() ok + health ok
                             │                                 ▼
                      crash loop exceeds   ┌────────────── ACTIVE ◀──────── recovered ─────┐
                      breaker threshold    │                 │  │                           │
                             │             │   plan removes/ │  │ health fails / partial     │
                        QUARANTINED ◀──────┘   disable       │  └──────────────▶ DEGRADED ──┘
                             │ manual release                ▼
                             └──────────────────────────▶ DRAINING ──drained or deadline──▶ STOPPING
                                                                                               │ deactivate() / kill
                                                             revoke (any state) ──────────────▶│
                                                                                               ▼
                                                                                            STOPPED ──▶ (absent)
```

| State | Accepts new invocations | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| PENDING | no | Artifact download and digest check |
| RESOLVED | queued (lazy start) | Nothing running yet; no cost |
| STARTING | queued (bounded, 10 s) | Sandbox spawn → handshake → `activate` |
| ACTIVE | yes | |
| DEGRADED | yes, with breaker in half-open | Health check failing or some instances crashed |
| DRAINING | no; in-flight calls finish | Deadline = `lifecycle.drainTimeoutMs` (default 30 s) |
| STOPPING | no | `deactivate()`, then SIGTERM, then SIGKILL |
| FAILED | no | Retried with backoff 1 s → 5 min |
| QUARANTINED | no | Circuit breaker tripped. Owning team is paged. Needs manual release. |

### 5.2 Hooks

All hooks are defined in `plugin-api.d.ts`. Timeouts come from the manifest `lifecycle` block, capped by host maximums.

| Hook | Required | When it runs | Timeout (default / max) | Contract |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `activate(ctx, info)` | **yes** | Load, and on the new instance during reload | 10 s / 60 s | Returns a `Contributions` object whose keys must **exactly** match manifest `contributes`, or activation fails. Must not perform user-scoped work, because no principal exists yet. May warm caches or open pools using *installation* config. |
| `deactivate(reason)` | no | Unload, disable, reload (old instance), host shutdown | 5 s / 30 s | Flush and close. Must be idempotent. The process is killed at the deadline regardless. |
| `snapshotState()` | no | Reload, on the old instance *before* drain | 2 s / 10 s | Returns `{ schemaVersion, data }` where `data` is JSON ≤ 1 MB. Only called if `lifecycle.reload.stateful`. |
| `healthCheck()` | no | Every 15 s while ACTIVE/DEGRADED | 2 s | `ok`, `degraded`, or `failing`, plus a detail. Three consecutive `failing` results trigger a restart. |
| `onConfigChanged(next, prev)` | no | Installation config updated | 5 s | Return `"applied"` to hot-apply, or `"reload-required"` and the supervisor does a reload. Omitting the hook means reload. |
| `migrateParams(from, params)` | per contribution, if `paramsSchemaVersion > 1` | Saved report loads an older params version | 2 s | Must be pure and deterministic. |

`ActivationInfo` tells the plugin *why* it is starting: `reason: "install" | "enable" | "upgrade" | "reload" | "restart" | "scale-out"`, `previousVersion?`, `previousState?`, `negotiatedApiVersion`, and `features`.

### 5.3 Load sequence

```
Supervisor                         Sandbox runtime                      Plugin
    │ spawn(container, limits)           │                                 │
    │──────────────────────────────────▶ │ start, open channel             │
    │ ◀── plugin.hello {protocols:[1], sdkVersion, apiRange} ──│           │
    │ ── host.hello {protocol:1, apiVersion:"1.3.0", features[], limits} ─▶│
    │                                    │ require(main) (≤ activation budget)
    │ ── plugin.activate {installationConfig, info} ──────────▶│ activate(ctx, info)
    │                                    │                                 │── returns Contributions
    │ ◀── result {contributions: {datasource:["netsuite"]}} ───│           │
    │ verify contributions == manifest                         │           │
    │ ── plugin.healthCheck ─────────────▶│ (if defined)                    │
    │ mark ACTIVE, route traffic         │                                 │
```

**API version negotiation.** The host picks the highest version that is in both the plugin's `engines.pluginApi` range and the host's supported set. If there is no overlap, the plugin goes to FAILED with `E_API_INCOMPATIBLE`. The resolver prevents this in normal operation, so hitting it is a bug.

### 5.4 Unload sequence
1. Remove the pool from the router so no new invocations arrive.
2. Enter DRAINING and wait for in-flight invocations, up to `drainTimeoutMs`. Invocations still running at the deadline get `$/cancel`, and 2 s later they fail with `E_UNAVAILABLE, retryable: true`.
3. STOPPING: call `deactivate({ reason })` with its timeout, then SIGTERM, wait 2 s, then SIGKILL the container.
4. Delete scratch tmpfs. KV data is kept, because it belongs to the installation, not the instance.

### 5.5 Reload (blue/green, zero downtime)

Reload is triggered by an upgrade, a config change that returned `reload-required`, a manual `rplug reload` in dev, or a crash restart. For a crash restart the old instance is already dead, so no snapshot is taken.

```
 1. Start GREEN instance(s) of the new version → STARTING (BLUE keeps serving)
 2. If stateful: BLUE.snapshotState() → S   (BLUE keeps serving during snapshot)
 3. GREEN.activate(ctx, {reason:"reload"|"upgrade", previousVersion, previousState:S})
      - GREEN must accept S.schemaVersion ≤ its own; unknown newer → treat as no state
 4. GREEN.healthCheck() ok  → atomically switch router to GREEN
      else                   → stop GREEN, BLUE untouched, emit ReloadFailed, pool stays on BLUE
 5. BLUE → DRAINING → STOPPING (deactivate reason:"reload")
```

Guarantees:
- **No request is lost.** Invocations that started on BLUE finish on BLUE, and new ones go to GREEN.
- **Rollback is automatic** when GREEN fails to start. An upgrade the supervisor rolls back is recorded against the release, and after 3 rollbacks across the fleet the release is auto-yanked.
- **The state snapshot is best-effort.** Plugins must still work correctly with `previousState` undefined. Durable state belongs in `inv.kv` (§6.3), not in memory.
- In dev, `rplug dev` watches files and triggers a reload on every build, so teams exercise this path all day.

### 5.6 Activation policy and scaling
- `activationEvents` (for example `onDatasource:netsuite`, `onStartup`) decides when a pool starts. The default is lazy start on first invocation. `onStartup` is only for plugins that other plugins depend on for services.
- The pool scales between `runtime.minInstances` and `maxInstances`. Each instance serves at most `runtime.concurrency` invocations at a time. The pool scales out when queue wait p95 exceeds 250 ms and scales in when an instance has been idle past `idleTimeoutSeconds`.
- Pools are per host replica. There is no cross-replica instance sharing.

### 5.7 Failure handling
- **Crash** (process exit, missed heartbeat ×3 at a 5 s interval, or OOM kill): in-flight invocations fail with `E_UNAVAILABLE, retryable: true`, and the instance restarts with backoff.
- **Circuit breaker** per pool: 5 crashes or 50% invocation failures (with at least 20 calls) in 60 s opens the breaker. While open, calls fail fast. A half-open probe runs after 30 s. Three consecutive opens within 15 min put the pool in QUARANTINED.
- **Report-level isolation.** The report engine treats each widget and pipeline branch independently. A failed plugin produces an error placeholder in that widget, and the rest of the report renders. Scheduled exports fail the whole job only if the exporter or delivery step itself failed.

## 6. Sandboxed execution boundary

### 6.1 Threat model

| Threat | Example | Primary mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Buggy plugin: crash, leak, infinite loop | `while(true)` in a transform | Process isolation, cgroup limits, deadlines, breaker |
| Compromised npm dependency | Postinstall-free malware in a bundled dependency that exfiltrates data | No network namespace, egress only through a broker allowlist, SBOM and scan, signing |
| Cross-tenant data leak | Module-level cache keyed wrongly, serving tenant A's rows to tenant B | `perTenant` isolation by default (§6.4) |
| Confused deputy | Plugin queries datasets the invoking user can't see | Broker enforces *user authority ∩ plugin grant* |
| SSRF | Egress to `169.254.169.254` or internal services | DNS pinning, private-range blocking, redirect re-check |
| Host DoS | Huge outputs, log floods, RPC floods | Size limits, rate limits, credit-based streams |
| Malicious output | XSS through an SVG or a crafted PDF | Output validators and sanitizer (§6.5) |
| Secret leakage | Plugin logs its API token | Secrets only via `inv.secrets`; host redacts known secret values from logs |
| Sandbox escape | Kernel exploit from the plugin process | gVisor (user-space kernel) in prod, seccomp, non-root, no capabilities |

Design stance: **internal teams write the plugins, but the sandbox is built for untrusted code.** The realistic risks are bugs and supply-chain compromise, and a boundary that is only designed for trusted code does nothing against either.

### 6.2 Isolation layers (defense in depth)

**L1: Process.** One OS process per instance. There is no shared memory with the host, and the only link to it is one RPC channel (a Unix domain socket, or a named pipe on Windows dev). stdout and stderr are captured as logs.

**L2: OS confinement (production, Linux).**
- Runtime: gVisor `runsc`. nsjail is the lighter alternative if gVisor's overhead turns out to be unacceptable after benchmarking.
- **No network namespace interfaces except loopback.** Every egress goes through the broker.
- Read-only root filesystem containing the Node runtime, `plugin-runtime`, and the plugin bundle, mounted read-only from the verified CAS digest.
- Writable `tmpfs` scratch at `/tmp`, capped at `limits.scratchBytes` (default 256 MB) and wiped on stop.
- Non-root UID, all Linux capabilities dropped, `no_new_privs`, default seccomp profile.
- cgroups v2: `memory.max`, `cpu.max`, `pids.max = 64`.

**L3: Runtime.**
`node --permission --allow-fs-read=/plugin,/runtime --allow-fs-write=/tmp --disallow-code-generation-from-strings --max-old-space-size=<limit*0.8>`
With `--permission`, child processes, workers, native addons, and WASI are denied unless explicitly allowed, and none are allowed. The Node permission model is **not** treated as a security boundary on its own (Node's docs say so too). It exists to give clear `ERR_ACCESS_DENIED` errors in dev mode, where L2 is absent.

**L4: Capability Broker.** This is the real enforcement point. It is described in §6.3.

**L5: Output validation.** Every result crossing back is validated (§6.5).

**Dev mode** (`rplug dev` on macOS or Windows): L1, L3, L4, and L5 are on, and L2 is replaced by best-effort limits. The CLI shows a banner saying the sandbox is relaxed. **The conformance suite in CI always runs with L2 on**, so anything that only works without it fails before publish.

### 6.3 Capability Broker

Every host-provided service a plugin uses is an RPC call to the broker. For each call, the broker:

1. **Authenticates the channel.** Each instance gets its own socket, so the plugin identity comes from the connection and not from the message.
2. **Checks the grant.** The permission must be in the installation Grant, not just requested in the manifest.
3. **Checks the principal.** For user-scoped operations, the invoking principal (from the invocation the call is nested under) must have the authority too. Calls outside an invocation only get installation-scoped services.
4. **Applies quotas and rate limits.**
5. **Audits** sensitive operations: secret reads, data queries, and egress destinations are sampled at 100% for revoked or quarantined plugins and at 1% otherwise.

| Permission (manifest `permissions`) | Broker surface | Enforcement detail |
|---|---|---|
| `network.egress[]` `{host, ports, methods?}` | `inv.fetch(url, init)` (WHATWG fetch subset) | Host glob match (`*.netsuite.com`); resolve DNS then block RFC1918, loopback, link-local, CGNAT, and metadata ranges; connect to the pinned IP; re-check every redirect (max 5); TLS required unless `allowInsecure` (dev only); response body cap `limits.maxFetchBytes`; 50 req/s per instance |
| `secrets[]` (names) | `inv.secrets.get(name)` | Only names declared **and** present in installation config fields marked `"x-secret": true`. Values are registered with the log redactor. |
| `storage.kv` `{quotaBytes}` | `inv.kv.get/set/delete/list` | Namespaced by `(installation, tenant)`. TTL supported. Quota enforced on write. |
| `data.query` `{datasets: "invoker"}` | `inv.data.query(sql or AST)` | Runs **as the invoking principal** with row-level security applied. Plugins can never query as a service account. The only allowed value in v1 is `"invoker"`. |
| `reports.read` | `inv.reports.get(id)` | As the invoker |
| `services[]` (implicit from `dependencies`) | `inv.services.get(pluginId, service)` | Callee grant applies. Depth ≤ 4. Cycles are detected. |
| *(always granted)* | `ctx.log`, `ctx.metrics`, `inv.signal`, `inv.deadline` | Log rate 100 lines/s with a burst of 500, line ≤ 16 KB. Metric cardinality ≤ 1000 series per plugin. |

A plugin running inside the sandbox has **no other way** to reach anything: there is no network, no writable filesystem outside scratch, and no child processes.

### 6.4 Tenant isolation
`runtime.isolation`:
- **`perTenant`** (default): pools are keyed by `(plugin@version, tenantId)`, so module-level state can never mix tenants. It costs more processes, which lazy activation and `idleTimeoutSeconds` offset.
- **`shared`**: one pool serves all tenants. This is only allowed if the plugin declares **no** `data.query`, `storage.kv`, `reports.read`, or `secrets` permissions, **and** platform has set a registry flag after review. It suits stateless renderers and format exporters, where process count matters.

Even in `shared` mode, every invocation carries its principal, and brokered services are still tenant-scoped.

### 6.5 Output validation

| Extension point | Validation |
|---|---|
| datasource / transform | Arrow schema of every batch == declared/returned schema; row count and byte caps; string length caps (1 MB per cell) |
| visualization | Vega-Lite: schema-validate, strip `data.url`, `usermeta`, and `href` encodings, disallow `expr` functions outside an allowlist. SVG: DOMPurify-style allowlist sanitization, strip external refs, size ≤ 5 MB |
| exporter | Magic-byte MIME check matches a declared type; `maxOutputBytes`; PDF: reject embedded JavaScript and launch actions |
| delivery | Receipt schema; `externalId` length cap |
| all | JSON results schema-validated against `plugin-api` wire schemas; unknown fields dropped (tolerant reader) |

### 6.6 Resource limits (defaults and hard maximums)

| Limit | Manifest key | Default | Max without platform approval |
|---|---|---|---|
| Memory per instance | `runtime.limits.memoryMb` | 512 | 2048 |
| CPU per instance | `runtime.limits.cpu` | 1.0 | 2.0 |
| Concurrency per instance | `runtime.concurrency` | 4 | 32 |
| Instances per pool | `runtime.maxInstances` | 4 | 16 |
| Invocation deadline | `contributes.*[].timeoutMs` | per EP (§3) | 2× default |
| Scratch disk | `runtime.limits.scratchBytes` | 256 MB | 2 GB |
| Output size | `runtime.limits.maxOutputBytes` | 100 MB | 1 GB |
| Fetch response size | `runtime.limits.maxFetchBytes` | 50 MB | 500 MB |
| Package size | (registry) | 50 MB | 200 MB |

The host always applies `min(requested, installation override, hard max)`.

## 7. Versioned API contract

### 7.1 Four version axes, each independent

| Axis | Format | Declared in | Changes when |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Plugin API** | semver `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` | `engines.pluginApi` (range) | The TS contract / wire method schemas change |
| **Wire protocol** | integer | `engines.protocol` (SDK sets it automatically) | Framing, handshake, or stream mechanics change |
| **Manifest schema** | integer | `manifestVersion` | The manifest shape changes |
| **Plugin release** | semver | `version` | The team ships |
| **Contribution params** | integer | `contributes.*[].paramsSchemaVersion` | A saved-report params shape changes (§3.6) |

Teams normally touch only the plugin release version and `paramsSchemaVersion`. The SDK version pins the other axes.

### 7.2 Compatibility rules for the Plugin API

**Minor (additive) — allowed:**
- New optional methods on an extension-point interface. The host checks for them before calling, and the SDK exposes `ctx.features.has()`.
- New optional fields in requests sent to plugins. Plugins **must ignore unknown fields**, and the SDK enforces this.
- New optional fields in plugin responses. The host ignores them if it runs an older minor.
- New host services on `ctx`/`inv`, gated behind a feature flag.
- New extension points.
- New error codes, as long as they map onto an existing category (§7.5).
- New enum values, **only** in enums documented as *open*, which plugins must handle with a default branch.

**Major (breaking) — only these:**
- Removing or renaming a method, field, service, or extension point.
- Making an optional field or method required.
- Changing a type, its semantics, or a default.
- Adding values to *closed* enums.
- Tightening validation of plugin outputs in a way that rejects previously valid output.

**Patch:** documentation, SDK bug fixes, and type-only corrections that don't change the wire format.

### 7.3 Support window and deprecation
- The host supports **the current major and the previous major for at least 12 months** after the new major reaches GA. Within a supported major, every minor is supported, because minors are additive.
- A feature slated for removal is marked `@deprecated` in the `.d.ts` file, at which point:
  - `rplug validate` warns about it
  - a `plugin_api_deprecated_calls_total{plugin,feature}` metric is emitted
  - owners get a notice at least **2 quarters** before the next major that removes it
- **Host implementation:** the host's internal domain model is *not* the plugin API. Each supported major has an **adapter layer**, `api/v1/*` and `api/v2/*`, that translates to the internal model. That is what makes the 12-month window affordable.
- **Experimental surface:** anything under the `experimental` namespace in the `.d.ts` file requires `engines.experimental: ["feature-name"]` in the manifest, can change in any minor, and **cannot be published to the `stable` channel**.

### 7.4 Wire protocol v1

**Transport:** one bidirectional stream per instance (UDS or named pipe).

**Framing:** each frame has a 4-byte big-endian length, a 1-byte frame type, and a payload.
- `0x01` CONTROL: UTF-8 JSON-RPC 2.0 message
- `0x02` DATA: 8-byte stream ID followed by an Arrow IPC stream message (schema or record batch)
- `0x03` BLOB: 8-byte stream ID followed by a raw chunk of up to 1 MB, used for exporter output and delivery attachments

**Handshake:** see §5.3. Nothing but `plugin.hello` and `host.hello` is accepted until both have been exchanged.

**Method namespaces:**

| Direction | Methods |
|---|---|
| host → plugin | `plugin.activate`, `plugin.deactivate`, `plugin.snapshotState`, `plugin.healthCheck`, `plugin.configChanged`, `plugin.migrateParams`, `invoke` |
| plugin → host | `host.fetch`, `host.secrets.get`, `host.kv.*`, `host.data.query`, `host.reports.get`, `host.services.call`, `host.log`, `host.metrics` |
| either | `$/cancel {id}`, `$/ping`, `$/pong`, `stream.open`, `stream.credit {id, n}`, `stream.end`, `stream.error` |

**`invoke` params:**
```json
{
  "extensionPoint": "datasource",
  "contribution": "netsuite",
  "method": "query",
  "params": { "...": "method-specific, schema in plugin-api" },
  "context": {
    "invocationId": "01J8…", "traceparent": "00-…-01",
    "principal": { "tenantId": "t_123", "userId": "u_456", "kind": "user" },
    "deadline": "2026-09-15T12:00:30.000Z",
    "locale": "en-US", "timeZone": "America/New_York",
    "callChain": ["@finance/netsuite-connector"],
    "idempotencyKey": null
  }
}
```

**Cancellation:** if the deadline passes or the caller aborts, the host sends `$/cancel`, which fires `inv.signal` in the plugin. The host stops waiting after the deadline plus a 2 s grace period. If the plugin keeps burning CPU for 10 s after cancellation, the instance is recycled.

**Backpressure:** streams are credit-based. The receiver grants N batches with `stream.credit`, and the sender must not exceed its credit. The default initial credit is 4 batches, and the target batch size is 64 k rows or 8 MB.

### 7.5 Error model

Every error carries `{ code, message, retryable, details? }`. The SDK exports the `PluginError` class and the code constants.

| Code | Category | Retryable default | Typical source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `E_INVALID_INPUT` | client | no | Bad params or spec |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | client | no | Missing table, report, or target |
| `E_PERMISSION_DENIED` | client | no | Broker denial, or upstream 403 |
| `E_UNAUTHENTICATED` | client | no | Bad or expired upstream credentials |
| `E_CONFLICT` | client | no | Idempotency key reused with different payload |
| `E_UNSUPPORTED` | client | no | Method or feature not implemented |
| `E_RATE_LIMITED` | transient | yes (honor `retryAfterMs`) | Upstream or broker rate limit |
| `E_TIMEOUT` | transient | yes | Deadline exceeded |
| `E_UNAVAILABLE` | transient | yes | Upstream down, or instance crashed |
| `E_RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` | transient | yes | Quota, memory, or output cap |
| `E_UPSTREAM` | transient | plugin decides | Other upstream failure |
| `E_INTERNAL` | bug | no | Uncaught exception (the SDK wraps it) |
| `E_API_INCOMPATIBLE` | host | no | Version negotiation failed |

Errors are mapped onto JSON-RPC error codes -32000 through -32099. User-facing messages come from `message`, and stack traces are captured to logs only, never returned to end users.

### 7.6 Data plane
Tabular data is **Apache Arrow** end to end. The SDK gives plugins `TableStream` (an async iterable of `RecordBatch` plus a schema) and helpers (`fromRows`, `toRows`, `collect`) for teams who don't need columnar performance.

Rationale: JSON serialization of large result sets would dominate latency across a process boundary. Arrow IPC is close to zero-copy on each side and language-neutral if a non-JS runtime is ever added.

### 7.7 Conformance as the definition of the contract
The `.d.ts` file is the human-readable contract. The **conformance suite** (§9.3) is the executable one. A behavior that isn't covered by the conformance suite isn't guaranteed. Any change to the API must include conformance tests, and the suite for every supported minor runs against the host in CI.

## 8. Observability

| Signal | What the host emits | Labels |
|---|---|---|
| Traces | Span per invocation (`plugin.invoke`), child spans per broker call; W3C `traceparent` propagated into the plugin, so SDK spans nest correctly | plugin, version, contribution, method, tenant (hashed) |
| Metrics | `plugin_invocations_total{outcome,code}`, `plugin_invocation_duration_seconds`, `plugin_queue_wait_seconds`, `plugin_instance_memory_bytes`, `plugin_instance_cpu_seconds_total`, `plugin_restarts_total{reason}`, `plugin_breaker_state`, `plugin_broker_denials_total{permission}`, `plugin_api_deprecated_calls_total` | plugin, version, owner_team |

## 9. Developer experience

### 9.1 Packages
- `@reporting/plugin-sdk`: types (`plugin-api.d.ts`), `definePlugin`, `PluginError`, Arrow helpers, and the in-sandbox runtime.
- `@reporting/plugin-testkit`: an in-memory fake host with a scriptable broker (fake fetch, KV, secrets, data), a principal builder, a clock, and fault injection (deadline, cancel, crash).
- `@reporting/rplug`: the CLI.

### 9.2 CLI

```
rplug init --type datasource|transform|visualization|exporter|delivery   scaffold with tests
rplug validate            manifest schema, contributions ⇄ exports, deprecations, limit sanity
rplug dev                 local host + sandbox (relaxed L2), hot reload, sample report UI
rplug test                unit tests via testkit
rplug conformance         run the official suite for the declared engines range
rplug pack                reproducible tarball (.rplug): manifest.json, dist/, sbom.json
rplug sign                sign with team key (CI: keyless OIDC via Sigstore)
rplug publish --channel   upload; streams verification report
rplug promote | yank      release management
rplug reload <id>         dev/staging only
```

### 9.3 Conformance suite (per extension point)
Examples of what it checks:
- **Lifecycle:** `activate` returns exactly the declared contributions. `deactivate` is idempotent. A reload with and without `previousState` both work. The plugin survives `previousState` with an unknown `schemaVersion`.
- **Datasource:** `query` respects `inv.signal` within 2 s. Stream schema matches `discoverSchema`. Declared pushdowns produce the same results as host-side execution on a fixture.
- **Transform:** `outputSchema` returns within 2 s without broker calls and is consistent with what `execute` produces.
- **Visualization:** output passes the sanitizer unchanged. A plugin whose output gets modified by sanitization fails, so teams see the problem early.
- **Exporter:** output MIME matches the declaration, and output is deterministic for fixed input with a fixed clock.
- **Delivery:** a repeated `idempotencyKey` returns the same receipt and has no second side effect.
- **Tolerant reader:** requests carrying random extra fields still succeed.
- **Sandbox:** in L2 mode, direct network, filesystem writes outside `/tmp`, and `child_process` all fail. Brokered fetch to a host that isn't allowlisted returns `E_PERMISSION_DENIED`.
- **Params migration:** `migrateParams` handles every `paramsSchemaVersion` from 1 to the current one on recorded fixtures.

### 9.4 Plugin package layout
```
my-plugin/
  manifest.json
  src/index.ts          export default definePlugin({ activate, deactivate, ... })
  src/contributions/…
  test/…
  fixtures/params/v1.json, v2.json     # for migrateParams conformance
  dist/index.js         # single bundled ESM file (esbuild); no node_modules at runtime
```
Bundling into one file is **required**. It makes the read-only root filesystem simple, loading fast, and the SBOM exact, since it is generated at bundle time.

## 10. Governance for five teams

- **Contract ownership.** The platform team owns the plugin API, the manifest schema, and the conformance suite. Changes go through a lightweight RFC: a PR to `docs/plugin-architecture/rfcs/`, review by platform plus one rotating plugin-team reviewer, and a 1-week comment period. Additive minors can be fast-tracked.
- **Namespaces.** Each team gets a namespace on day one (for example `@finance`, `@ops`, `@growth`). Cross-team shared services go under `@platform` or a jointly owned namespace with an explicit owner.
- **Operational ownership.** The owning team is on the hook for its plugins' alerts (breaker open, quarantine, error-rate SLO). Platform is on the hook for the host, broker, sandbox, and registry.
- **Default SLOs per plugin** (teams may tighten them): 99.5% non-client-error success, and p95 latency within 50% of the extension point's deadline.
- **Release policy.** Stable releases require CI provenance and a passing conformance run. Only platform or security can revoke.
- **Shared learning.** Keep a `#reporting-plugins` channel, hold office hours, and maintain one reference plugin per extension point in the SDK repo, kept green against every API minor.

## 11. Delivery plan

The critical path is **freezing the contract and shipping the SDK and dev host before the teams start**. Teams can build against the testkit and relaxed dev host while the production sandbox and registry are still being hardened.

| Phase | Deliverables | Exit criteria |
|---|---|---|
| **P0: Contract freeze** (before the quarter) | This design approved. `plugin-api.d.ts` v1.0.0-rc and `manifest.schema.json` v1 frozen. Wire protocol v1 spec. | Sign-off from all 5 teams after each has sketched its plugin against the `.d.ts` file |
| **P1: SDK and dev loop** (weeks 1–3) | `plugin-sdk`, `plugin-testkit`, `rplug init/validate/dev/test/pack`, reference plugins for all 5 extension points, conformance suite v1 | Each team scaffolds and runs a plugin locally in week 1 |
| **P2: Host runtime** (weeks 2–7) | Supervisor and state machine, instance pool, router, broker (all permissions), output validators, Arrow data plane, blue/green reload, breaker, observability | Reference plugins pass conformance on the real host with L2. Chaos tests (kill -9, OOM, hang) pass. |
| **P3: Registry** (weeks 3–8) | Registry API, verification pipeline, signing, resolver and plans, grants and permission diff, yank/revoke, audit | End-to-end: publish → install → grant → plan → host loads, in staging |
| **P4: Pilot** (weeks 6–9) | One team's plugin in prod on the `beta` channel for allowlisted tenants | 2 weeks meeting SLO, 1 successful zero-downtime upgrade, 1 rehearsed revoke |
| **P5: GA v1.0.0** (weeks 9–10) | API 1.0.0 final, `stable` channel open, runbooks, dashboards | All 5 teams able to publish to stable |
| **P6: Hardening** (rest of the quarter) | gVisor performance tuning, `shared` isolation review process, bulk report migration tool | — |

**Biggest schedule risk:** the teams discover a missing API surface mid-quarter. Mitigation: the P0 sign-off requires each team to write its real plugin's skeleton against the `.d.ts` file. Gaps found later go into `experimental` in a minor release within about 1 week, not into a major.

# Plugin Architecture for the Reporting Tool: Design v1.0

## 0. Assumptions

| # | Assumption | If wrong, revisit |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | The host is a server-side TypeScript/Node service | §6 runtime layer, SDK |
| A2 | Production runs on Linux containers (e.g. Kubernetes) | §6 OS confinement |
| A3 | Multi-tenant: many customers share one deployment | §6.4 tenant isolation |
| A4 | Tabular data flows source → transform → chart/export | §7.6 data plane |
| A5 | v1 runs no plugin code in the end user's browser | §3 visualizations |
| A6 | The five teams are internal; third-party plugins may come later | §6 threat model |

## 1. Goals and non-goals

**Goals**
1. **Parallel work.** Five teams build against a frozen contract without coordinating with each other.
2. **Fault containment.** A plugin that crashes, hangs or leaks memory breaks only the widgets that use it. The host, other plugins and other tenants keep working.
3. **Least privilege.** A plugin reaches only what it declared and an admin granted. It never gets more authority than the user who invoked it.
4. **Zero-downtime lifecycle.** Install, upgrade, reload and revoke all happen without restarting the host.
5. **Long-lived compatibility.** Saved reports outlive plugin versions, and plugins outlive host API versions.
6. **Operability.** Every invocation is traced and attributed to the team that owns the plugin.

**Non-goals for v1:** plugin JS in the browser, native addons, an in-process "trusted" fast path, a third-party marketplace, and plugins that extend other plugins' extension points. Plugins can still call each other's services through the host (§4.5).

## 2. Architecture

```
┌───────────────────────── Control plane ─────────────────────────┐
│ rplug CLI ─publish─▶ Registry API ─▶ Verification ─▶ Artifact    │
│ Admin UI ─install──▶ (Postgres)      pipeline        store (CAS) │
│                          │                                        │
│                      Resolver ─▶ Resolved Plan (per environment)  │
└──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┘
                           │ watch (hosts never call registry on hot path)
┌──────────────────────── Host (N replicas) ───────────────────────┐
│ Report engine ─▶ Extension Point Router ─▶ Supervisor ─▶ Instance │
│      ▲                                      (lifecycle,   Pools   │
│ Output validators ◀─────────────────────    breaker)       │      │
│                         Capability Broker ◀────────────────┤ RPC  │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────┘
                  ┌──── Sandbox (one per instance) ──────────┴──┐
                  │ gVisor container: no net, RO rootfs, cgroups │
                  │   node --permission plugin-runtime + bundle  │
                  └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The control plane and data plane are separate. If the registry goes down, hosts keep running their last applied Resolved Plan, with artifacts cached locally and checked against their digests.

| Component | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| Registry API | Publishers, releases, installations, grants, audit log |
| Verification pipeline | Gates each release before it can be installed (§4.2) |
| Resolver | Produces a deterministic, diffable Resolved Plan per environment |
| Supervisor | Lifecycle state machine, reconciling the plan against running state, restarts, circuit breaker, draining |
| Instance Pool | Scales sandboxed instances and routes invocations to them |
| Router | Maps a report's contribution reference to a pool; runs params migration |
| Capability Broker | The only path from a plugin to the outside world; enforces permissions |
| Output validators | Treat every plugin output as untrusted |
| plugin-runtime | Shim inside the sandbox: protocol, handshake, dispatch |

## 3. Extension points (v1)

Each contribution is addressed by a fully qualified contribution ID, `@finance/netsuite-connector:netsuite`. Plugin IDs are namespaced per team, so contribution IDs can't collide.

| Extension point | Methods | Input → Output | Default deadline |
|---|---|---|---|
| `datasource` | `testConnection`, `discoverSchema`, `query`, `estimate?` | config + query → Arrow stream | 300 s |
| `transform` | `validateParams`, `outputSchema`, `execute` | params + N Arrow streams → Arrow stream | 120 s |
| `visualization` | `validateSpec`, `dataRequirements`, `render` | spec + table → Vega-Lite spec **or** sanitized SVG | 30 s |
| `exporter` | `export` | report document → file (PDF, XLSX…) | 180 s |
| `delivery` | `validateTarget`, `deliver` | files + target → receipt | 60 s |

Rules for each extension point:
- **Datasource pushdown.** The manifest declares which operations the source can execute itself (`filter`, `project`, `sort`, `limit`, `aggregate`).
  - The host sends only declared operations, and the plugin must apply everything it receives.
  - If a filter contains an operator the plugin doesn't recognize, it throws `E_UNSUPPORTED`. The host then filters on its side. This lets new filter operators be added in a minor version.
- **Transform `outputSchema`** must be pure and return within 2 s. The editor calls it on every edit. The host checks the batches from `execute` against this schema.
- **Visualizations return declarative output only.** Plugin JS never runs in browsers, which removes the need for a second, browser-side sandbox. Custom interactive widgets would be a separate v2 "client extension point".
- **Delivery idempotency.** `deliver` receives an `idempotencyKey`. A repeated key must be a no-op that returns the original receipt, because scheduled deliveries are retried.

**Saved-report compatibility.** This matters a lot for a reporting tool.
- Saved reports store `{fqcid, pluginMajor, paramsSchemaVersion, params}`.
- A contribution that raises `paramsSchemaVersion` must implement `migrateParams(from, params)`. The router runs it lazily when an older report loads.
- A report that references a missing, disabled or revoked plugin shows an "unavailable" placeholder. The report is never deleted or corrupted.
- Pinning to `pluginMajor` means a new plugin major never silently changes saved reports. Admins upgrade reports explicitly with a bulk migration tool that reuses `migrateParams`.

## 4. Plugin registry

### 4.1 Identity and data model

Plugin IDs have the form `@<namespace>/<name>`. Namespaces map to owning teams, and only that team's signing keys can publish under a namespace. `@platform` is reserved.

```
Publisher    (namespace PK, team, contacts[], signingKeys[{keyId, publicKey, status, notAfter}])
Plugin       (id PK, namespace, displayName, archived)
Release      (pluginId, version) PK, digest sha256, manifest jsonb, signature, provenance,
             sbom, status: pending|verifying|rejected|published|yanked|revoked,
             channel: dev|beta|stable, permissionDiff jsonb, verificationReport jsonb
Environment  (id, name, hostApiRange)
Installation (id, environmentId, pluginId, scope: global|tenant:<id>, versionConstraint|pin,
             channel, enabled, configRef, grantId)
Grant        (id, installationId, permissions jsonb ⊆ manifest request, approvedBy, approvedDigest)
ResolvedPlan (environmentId, generation PK, entries[{pluginId, version, digest, scopes, grantId}], cause)
AuditEvent   (append-only)
```

### 4.2 Publish pipeline

`rplug pack → sign → publish`, after which the registry runs these checks:
1. Upload to content-addressed storage (CAS).
2. Validate the manifest against its schema.
3. Verify the signature against the namespace's key.
4. The version must be new and higher than any published version. Releases are immutable.
5. Package lint:
   - no native addons
   - size ≤ 50 MB
   - declared contributions equal exported ones
6. SBOM present; a critical vulnerability blocks the release.
7. CI provenance attestation (required for `stable`).
8. The conformance suite runs **in the real sandbox** against every host API minor in the declared range.
9. Compute `permissionDiff` against the previous release.

**Channels.**
- `dev`: dev environments only.
- `beta`: staging, plus allowlisted production tenants.
- `stable`: everywhere.

Promotion only changes metadata on the same digest, so the bytes that were tested are the bytes that ship.

### 4.3 Installation and grants
- The admin approves a **subset** of the requested permissions. Anything not granted is denied at runtime.
- Permissions marked `required: true` must be granted, or installation fails.
- **Upgrades that add permissions** stop at the previous version and ask the installation's admins for approval. Upgrades that reduce permissions apply automatically.
- Config lives in the host's config store and secrets in the vault. The registry holds only references.

### 4.4 Resolution
1. **Pick candidates** for each enabled installation. A release qualifies if:
   - it satisfies the version constraint
   - its channel is allowed in the environment
   - it is `published`
   - its `engines.pluginApi` overlaps the environment's `hostApiRange`
   - its required permissions are granted
2. **Resolve dependencies** to the highest version that satisfies all dependents. Different majors of one plugin can run side by side, each as its own process.
3. **Fail closed per plugin.** Cycles and unsatisfiable graphs keep the affected plugins on their last good resolution. Everything else still resolves.
4. **Emit a new plan generation** with a readable diff. The process is deterministic, and the plan is the only thing hosts consume.

### 4.5 Dependencies between plugins
- A plugin can declare `provides.services[]`, each method described by a JSON Schema. Other plugins list it in `dependencies` and call `inv.services.get(id, name).call(method, args)`.
- All calls go **through the broker**. The callee runs under the *original user* and *its own* grant.
- Call depth is capped at 4, and cycles are detected.
- Load order is topological and unload order is the reverse. Reloading a dependency doesn't restart the plugins that depend on it.

### 4.6 Yank, revoke, archive

| Action | Effect | Who |
|---|---|---|
| Yank | No new resolutions pick the release; running instances continue | Owning team or platform |
| Revoke | Kill switch: removed from all plans; hosts force-unload within 60 s with no drain; dependents become DEGRADED | Platform or security only |
| Archive | No new releases or installs | Owning team |

### 4.7 Registry API (`/v1`)
```
POST  /v1/publishers/{ns}/keys
POST  /v1/plugins/{id}/releases                         (package, signature, attestation)
GET   /v1/plugins/{id}/releases/{version}
POST  /v1/plugins/{id}/releases/{version}:promote|:yank|:revoke
GET   /v1/plugins?namespace=&extensionPoint=&q=
POST  /v1/environments/{env}/installations
PATCH /v1/environments/{env}/installations/{id}
POST  /v1/environments/{env}/installations/{id}/grants
GET   /v1/environments/{env}/plan                        (ETag = generation)
GET   /v1/environments/{env}/plan:watch                  (SSE)
GET   /v1/audit?pluginId=&since=
```

## 5. Lifecycle

### 5.1 State machine
There is one state machine per pool, keyed by `pluginId@version[/tenant]`.

```
(absent) ─plan adds─▶ PENDING ─digest ok─▶ RESOLVED ─first call / onStartup─▶ STARTING
STARTING ─activate ok + healthy─▶ ACTIVE ⇄ DEGRADED (health / partial crash)
STARTING ─error/timeout─▶ FAILED ─backoff 1s→5min─▶ STARTING
ACTIVE ─plan removes / disable─▶ DRAINING ─done or deadline─▶ STOPPING ─▶ STOPPED ─▶ (absent)
breaker trips 3× in 15 min ─▶ QUARANTINED (pages owner; manual release)
revoke (any state) ─▶ STOPPING (no drain)
```

### 5.2 Hooks

| Hook | Required | Timeout (default/max) | Contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| `activate(ctx, info)` | **yes** | 10 s / 60 s | Returns `Contributions`, whose keys must **exactly** match manifest `contributes`. No user-scoped work here, since no user is attached yet. May warm connection pools. |
| `deactivate(reason)` | no | 5 s / 30 s | Idempotent flush and close. The process is killed at the deadline regardless. |
| `snapshotState()` | no | 2 s / 10 s | `{schemaVersion, data}` of at most 1 MB of JSON. Only called if `lifecycle.reload.stateful`. |
| `healthCheck()` | no | 2 s | Runs every 15 s. Three consecutive `failing` results trigger a restart. |
| `onConfigChanged(next, prev)` | no | 5 s | Returns `"applied"` or `"reload-required"`. If the hook is absent, the host reloads. |
| `migrateParams(from, params)` | if `paramsSchemaVersion > 1` | 2 s | Pure and deterministic. |

`ActivationInfo.reason` is one of `install | enable | upgrade | reload | restart | scale-out`. It also carries `previousVersion`, `previousState` and `negotiatedApiVersion`.

### 5.3 Load
1. The supervisor spawns the sandbox with its limits.
2. The plugin sends `plugin.hello` with its supported protocols, SDK version and API range.
3. The host replies with `host.hello`: the highest API version both sides support, feature flags and limits. If there's no overlap, the pool goes to FAILED with `E_API_INCOMPATIBLE`. The resolver should prevent this, so it indicates a bug.
4. The plugin runs `activate`.
5. The host verifies that the returned contributions match the manifest.
6. The host runs `healthCheck`, then marks the pool ACTIVE and routes traffic to it.

### 5.4 Unload
1. Remove the pool from the router.
2. Drain: in-flight calls get `drainTimeoutMs` (default 30 s). Calls still running at the deadline receive `$/cancel`, then fail 2 s later with `E_UNAVAILABLE, retryable`.
3. Call `deactivate`, send SIGTERM, wait 2 s, send SIGKILL.
4. Wipe the scratch space. KV data survives, because it belongs to the installation.

### 5.5 Reload (blue/green, zero downtime)
1. Start the GREEN instance while BLUE keeps serving.
2. If the plugin is stateful, call `BLUE.snapshotState()` to get snapshot S.
3. Call `GREEN.activate(ctx, {reason, previousVersion, previousState: S})`. If S has a newer schema version than GREEN understands, GREEN ignores it.
4. If GREEN is healthy, switch the router to it atomically. If not, stop GREEN and leave BLUE untouched.
5. BLUE drains, then stops with reason `reload`.

Guarantees:
- No request is lost: in-flight calls finish on BLUE.
- A failed GREEN rolls back automatically. After 3 fleet-wide rollbacks, the release is auto-yanked.
- The snapshot is best-effort. Plugins must still work with `previousState` undefined, and durable state belongs in `inv.kv`.
- `rplug dev` reloads the plugin on every build, so teams exercise this path all day.

### 5.6 Scaling and failure handling
- **Activation.** Pools start lazily on the first invocation. `onStartup` is only for plugins that provide services to others.
- **Scaling.** Pools run between `minInstances` and `maxInstances`, with `concurrency` calls per instance. They scale out when p95 queue wait exceeds 250 ms and scale in after `idleTimeoutSeconds`.
- **Crashes.** A crash is a process exit, OOM, or 3 missed heartbeats at 5 s intervals. In-flight calls fail with `E_UNAVAILABLE, retryable`, and the instance restarts with backoff.
- **Circuit breaker.** It opens after 5 crashes, or a failure rate of at least 50% over at least 20 calls, within 60 s. A half-open probe runs after 30 s.
- **Report-level isolation.** Each widget or pipeline branch fails on its own. A scheduled export fails only if the export or delivery step itself failed.

## 6. Sandboxed execution boundary

### 6.1 Threat model

| Threat | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Buggy plugin (crash, infinite loop, memory leak) | Separate process, cgroups, deadlines, circuit breaker |
| Compromised npm dependency exfiltrating data | No network namespace; outbound traffic only through the broker allowlist; SBOM scan; signing |
| Cross-tenant leak via module-level caches | `perTenant` isolation by default |
| Confused deputy | Broker enforces the invoking user's authority ∩ plugin grant |
| SSRF (internal services, cloud metadata endpoint) | DNS pinning, private-range blocking, every redirect re-checked |
| Host DoS (huge output, log floods) | Size caps, rate limits, credit-based streams |
| Malicious output (XSS via SVG, PDF JavaScript) | Output validators (§6.5) |
| Secret leakage in logs | Secrets only via the broker; host redacts secret values from logs |
| Sandbox escape | gVisor user-space kernel, seccomp, non-root, all Linux capabilities dropped |

The teams writing plugins are internal, but the boundary is still built for untrusted code. The realistic risks are bugs and supply-chain compromise, and a boundary that assumes trusted code stops neither.

### 6.2 Layers
- **L1: Process.** One OS process per instance. Its only link to the host is a single RPC channel (Unix socket, or named pipe in Windows dev). stdout and stderr are captured as logs.
- **L2: OS confinement** (prod Linux):
  - gVisor `runsc`; nsjail as a fallback if benchmarks demand it
  - loopback-only network
  - read-only rootfs mounted from the verified digest
  - `/tmp` tmpfs capped by `scratchBytes`
  - non-root, `no_new_privs`, seccomp
  - cgroups v2 limits on memory, CPU and `pids.max=64`
- **L3: Runtime flags.** `node --permission --allow-fs-read=/plugin,/runtime --allow-fs-write=/tmp --disallow-code-generation-from-strings`. No child processes, workers, native addons or WASI. Node itself says its permission model is not a security boundary. It's here to give clear errors in dev, where L2 is absent.
- **L4: Capability Broker.** This is the real enforcement point (§6.3).
- **L5: Output validation** (§6.5).

In **dev mode** (`rplug dev` on Windows or macOS), L2 is replaced by best-effort limits and the CLI shows a banner saying so. **CI conformance always runs with L2 on**, so code that works only without the full sandbox fails before it can be published.

### 6.3 Capability Broker
For each call, the broker:
1. Identifies the plugin by its channel, since each instance has its own socket, not by anything in the message.
2. Checks the **Grant**, not just the manifest request.
3. Checks the **invoking user's** authority.
4. Applies quotas.
5. Writes an audit record, sampled.

| Permission | API | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|
| `network.egress[] {host, ports, methods}` | `inv.fetch` | Host glob match; DNS resolved, then RFC1918/loopback/link-local/metadata ranges blocked; connects to the pinned IP; ≤5 redirects, each re-checked; TLS required; `maxFetchBytes` cap; 50 req/s |
| `secrets[] {name}` | `inv.secrets.get` | Only declared names that are `x-secret` fields in config. Values are fed to the log redactor. Secret fields in a datasource's own connection config are implicitly allowed for that datasource. |
| `storage.kv {quotaBytes}` | `inv.kv.*` | Namespaced per (installation, tenant); TTL supported; quota enforced on write |
| `data.query {as: "invoker"}` | `inv.data.query` | Always runs **as the invoking user**, with row-level security. There is no service-account mode. |
| `reports.read` | `inv.reports.get` | Runs as the invoking user |
| (from `dependencies`) | `inv.services.get` | The callee's grant applies; depth ≤ 4 |
| always granted | `ctx.log`, `ctx.metrics`, `inv.signal` | Logs: 100 lines/s with burst 500; metrics: ≤1000 series |

### 6.4 Tenant isolation
- **`perTenant`** is the default. Pools are keyed by (plugin@version, tenant), so module-level state can never mix tenants.
- **`shared`** requires two things:
  - the plugin declares **no** data, KV, reports or secrets permissions
  - platform sets a flag after review

  It's meant for stateless renderers and format exporters. Brokered calls are still tenant-scoped in either mode.

### 6.5 Output validation

| Extension point | Checks |
|---|---|
| datasource / transform | Every batch's Arrow schema matches the declared one; row and byte caps; cells ≤1 MB |
| visualization | **Vega-Lite:** schema-validated; `data.url`, `usermeta` and hrefs stripped; expression functions allowlisted. **SVG:** allowlist sanitizer, no `<script>`, `<foreignObject>`, event handlers or external refs; ≤5 MB |
| exporter | File magic bytes match a declared MIME type; `maxOutputBytes`; PDFs with JavaScript or launch actions rejected |
| all | Responses validated against the wire schemas; unknown fields dropped |

### 6.6 Limits

| Limit | Default | Max without platform approval |
|---|---|---|
| Memory / CPU per instance | 512 MB / 1.0 | 2048 MB / 2.0 |
| Concurrency / instances | 4 / 4 | 32 / 16 |
| Invocation deadline | per extension point (§3) | 2× default |
| Scratch / output / fetch body | 256 MB / 100 MB / 50 MB | 2 GB / 1 GB / 500 MB |
| Package size | 50 MB | 200 MB |

The effective limit is `min(requested, installation override, hard max)`.

## 7. Versioned API contract

### 7.1 Version axes

| Axis | Format | Declared in |
|---|---|---|
| Plugin API | semver | `engines.pluginApi` (range) |
| Wire protocol | integer | `engines.protocol` (set by the SDK) |
| Manifest schema | integer | `manifestVersion` |
| Plugin release | semver | `version` |
| Contribution params | integer | `contributes.*[].paramsSchemaVersion` |

Teams normally touch only the last two. The SDK version pins the rest.

### 7.2 Compatibility rules

**Minor (additive):**
- new optional methods, detected with `ctx.features.has()`
- new optional request or response fields; plugins **must ignore unknown fields**, and the SDK enforces this
- new host services behind feature flags
- new extension points
- new error codes that map to an existing category
- new values in enums documented as *open*, which plugins must handle with a default branch

**Major (breaking):**
- removing or renaming anything
- making an optional field or method required
- changing a type, its semantics or a default
- adding values to closed enums
- tightening output validation so previously valid output is rejected

**Patch:** docs, SDK fixes, type-only corrections.

### 7.3 Support and deprecation
- The host supports the **current and previous major for at least 12 months** after the new major's GA.
- Deprecation happens through `@deprecated` in the `.d.ts`. `rplug validate` warns, the `plugin_api_deprecated_calls_total` metric counts usage, and owners get **2 quarters' notice** before a removal.
- The host's internal model is **not** the plugin API. Each supported major has its own adapter layer (`api/v1`, `api/v2`), which keeps a 12-month support window affordable.
- **Experimental features.** The `experimental` namespace requires `engines.experimental: [...]`. It can change in any minor and can't be published to `stable`.

### 7.4 Wire protocol v1
- **Transport:** one duplex stream per instance.
- **Frame format:** a `u32` big-endian length, a `u8` type, then the payload. Types:
  - `0x01` JSON-RPC 2.0 control message
  - `0x02` stream ID + Arrow IPC message
  - `0x03` stream ID + blob chunk (≤1 MB)
- **Host → plugin:** `plugin.activate`, `plugin.deactivate`, `plugin.snapshotState`, `plugin.healthCheck`, `plugin.configChanged`, `plugin.migrateParams`, `invoke`
- **Plugin → host:** `host.fetch`, `host.secrets.get`, `host.kv.*`, `host.data.query`, `host.reports.get`, `host.services.call`, `host.log`, `host.metrics`
- **Either direction:** `$/cancel`, `$/ping`, `stream.open`, `stream.credit`, `stream.end`, `stream.error`

Example `invoke` context:
```json
{ "extensionPoint": "datasource", "contribution": "netsuite", "method": "query", "params": {},
  "context": { "invocationId": "01J8…", "traceparent": "00-…-01",
    "principal": { "kind": "user", "tenantId": "t_123", "userId": "u_456" },
    "deadline": "2026-09-15T12:00:30Z", "locale": "en-US", "timeZone": "America/New_York",
    "callChain": ["@finance/netsuite-connector"], "idempotencyKey": null } }
```

- **Cancellation.** `$/cancel` fires `inv.signal`. The host stops waiting at the deadline + 2 s. An instance still burning CPU 10 s after cancel is recycled.
- **Backpressure.** Streams are credit-based: initial credit is 4 batches, and batches target 64k rows or 8 MB.

### 7.5 Error model
Every error has the shape `{code, message, retryable, retryAfterMs?, details?}`.

| Code | Retryable |
|---|---|
| `E_INVALID_INPUT`, `E_NOT_FOUND`, `E_PERMISSION_DENIED`, `E_UNAUTHENTICATED`, `E_CONFLICT`, `E_UNSUPPORTED` | no |
| `E_RATE_LIMITED`, `E_TIMEOUT`, `E_UNAVAILABLE`, `E_RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` | yes |
| `E_UPSTREAM` | plugin decides |
| `E_INTERNAL` (uncaught exception, wrapped by the SDK), `E_API_INCOMPATIBLE` | no |

Codes map to JSON-RPC codes -32000 to -32099. Stack traces go to logs only, never to end users.

### 7.6 Data plane
Tables travel as **Apache Arrow** end to end. JSON serialization of large result sets would dominate latency across a process boundary, and Arrow is language-neutral if you add Python later. The SDK provides `fromRows`, `toRows` and `collect` helpers for teams that don't need columnar performance.

### 7.7 Conformance
The `.d.ts` file is the human-readable contract, and the conformance suite is the executable one. Behavior the suite doesn't test isn't guaranteed, so every API change must add conformance tests.

## 8. Observability
- **Traces.** A span per invocation, with child spans per broker call. `traceparent` is propagated into the plugin.
- **Metrics:**
  - `plugin_invocations_total{outcome,code}`
  - `plugin_invocation_duration_seconds`
  - `plugin_queue_wait_seconds`
  - `plugin_instance_memory_bytes`, `plugin_instance_cpu_seconds_total`
  - `plugin_restarts_total{reason}`
  - `plugin_breaker_state`
  - `plugin_broker_denials_total{permission}`
  - `plugin_api_deprecated_calls_total`

  All metrics carry `plugin`, `version` and **`owner_team`**, so alerts route to the owning team.
- **Logs.** Structured, with secrets redacted and rate limits applied. A dropped-lines counter records what the limiter discards.
- **Audit.** Every registry change, plus sampled sensitive broker calls.
- **Custom metrics.** Plugins get `ctx.metrics`, auto-prefixed and capped in cardinality.
- **Dashboards.** One is provisioned automatically for each plugin.

## 9. Developer experience
- **Packages:**
  - `@reporting/plugin-sdk`: types, `definePlugin`, `PluginError`, Arrow helpers, the runtime
  - `@reporting/plugin-testkit`: fake host with a scriptable broker, fault injection for deadlines, cancel and crashes
  - `@reporting/rplug`: the CLI
- **CLI:**
  ```
  init --type <ep> | validate | dev | test | conformance | pack | sign | publish --channel | promote | yank | reload
  ```
- **Conformance suite** (runs against every extension point):
  - `activate` returns exactly the declared contributions
  - reload works both with and without `previousState`, including an unknown state version
  - `query` honors `signal` within 2 s
  - `discoverSchema` matches what `query` streams
  - pushdown results equal host-side execution
  - `outputSchema` returns within 2 s with no broker calls
  - visualization output passes the sanitizer *unchanged*
  - exporter output matches its MIME type and is deterministic under a fixed clock
  - a repeated delivery idempotency key causes no second side effect
  - requests with random extra fields still succeed
  - with L2 on, direct network, file writes outside `/tmp` and `child_process` all fail
  - `migrateParams` handles every params version fixture
- **Package layout.** The manifest, a single esbuild ESM bundle in `dist/index.js` (required: no `node_modules` at runtime, and the SBOM is exact), plus `fixtures/params/v*.json`.

## 10. Governance for five teams
- **Platform owns the contract**: the API, the manifest schema and the conformance suite.
- **API changes go through an RFC.** Reviewers are platform plus one rotating plugin-team member, with a 1-week comment window. Additive minors can be fast-tracked.
- **Each team gets a namespace on day one.** Shared services live under `@platform` or have an explicitly named owner.
- **Operational split.** Owning teams take alerts for their plugins (breaker open, quarantine, SLO). Platform owns the host, broker, sandbox and registry.
- **Default SLO:** 99.5% success excluding client errors, and p95 latency ≤ 50% of the extension point's deadline.
- **Reference plugins.** Keep one per extension point in the SDK repo, green against every API minor.

## 11. Delivery plan
The critical path is **freezing the contract and shipping the SDK, testkit and dev host before the teams start.** They can then build while the production sandbox and registry are hardened.

| Phase | Deliverables | Exit criteria |
|---|---|---|
| P0 (before the quarter) | This design; `plugin-api.d.ts` 1.0.0-rc and manifest schema v1 frozen | All 5 teams have written their real plugin's skeleton against the `.d.ts` and signed off |
| P1 (wk 1–3) | SDK, testkit, `rplug init/validate/dev/test/pack`, 5 reference plugins, conformance v1 | Each team runs a plugin locally in week 1 |
| P2 (wk 2–7) | Supervisor, pools, router, broker, validators, Arrow data plane, blue/green reload, breaker, observability | Reference plugins pass conformance with L2 on; chaos tests (`kill -9`, OOM, hang) pass |
| P3 (wk 3–8) | Registry, verification, signing, resolver, grants, revoke, audit | Publish → install → grant → plan → load works end to end in staging |
| P4 (wk 6–9) | One team's plugin in prod on `beta` | 2 weeks within SLO; one zero-downtime upgrade; one rehearsed revoke |
| P5 (wk 9–10) | API 1.0.0 GA, `stable` channel open, runbooks | All 5 teams can publish to stable |

**Biggest risk:** teams find a missing API surface mid-quarter. Mitigation: the P0 skeleton requirement surfaces gaps early, and anything found later ships under `experimental` in a minor release within a week rather than waiting for a major.

## 12. Open decisions
1. **Confirm A1/A2 (Node + Linux containers).** If the product also runs on-prem or on Windows servers, L2 needs a separate design.
2. **Benchmark gVisor cold start.** If it exceeds ~800 ms, pre-warm hot pools or switch to nsjail.
3. **Declarative-only charts.** Is that enough for all five teams? If not, scope the browser extension point now; it needs its own sandbox.
4. **Region-constrained egress.** Is it needed for data residency?
5. **Python plugins.** Does any team need them (e.g. statistical transforms)? The protocol and Arrow already allow it.
6. **Principal for scheduled jobs.** Which user does a scheduled job run as, and what happens when that user leaves?

```json
    "service": {
      "type": "object", "additionalProperties": false, "required": ["name", "methods"],

        "methods": {

          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "object", "additionalProperties": false, "required": ["params", "result"],
            "properties": {

        }
      }
    },

    "contributionBase": {
      "type": "object", "required": ["id", "displayName"],
      "properties": {
        "id": { "$ref": "#/$defs/localId" },
        "displayName": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1, "maxLength": 80 },
        "description": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 500 },
        "icon": { "type": "string", "pattern": "^assets/[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+\\.svg$" },

```

JSON Schema can't express a few cross-field rules, so `rplug validate` and the registry check them:
- every `secrets[].name` is an `x-secret` property in `configSchema`
- `minInstances ≤ maxInstances` and `inputs.min ≤ inputs.max`
- `activationEvents` refer to declared contributions or services
- `isolation: "shared"` has no data, KV, reports or secrets permissions and carries the platform approval flag
- `paramsSchemaVersion > 1` has `fixtures/params/v1..vN`
- `timeoutMs` ≤ 2× the extension point's default

## Appendix B: API contract (`plugin-api.d.ts`, Plugin API v1.0.0)

```ts
// @reporting/plugin-sdk — Plugin API contract v1.0.0
// Rules: plugins MUST ignore unknown request fields; enums marked "open" MUST have a default branch.
import type { RecordBatch, Schema } from "apache-arrow";

// ───────────────────────── JSON ─────────────────────────
export type JsonPrimitive = string | number | boolean | null;
export type JsonValue = JsonPrimitive | JsonValue[] | { [k: string]: JsonValue };
export type JsonObject = { [k: string]: JsonValue };
export type PluginApiVersion = `${number}.${number}.${number}`;

// ───────────────────────── Entry point ─────────────────────────
export interface PluginDefinition<Config extends JsonObject = JsonObject> {
  /** Required. Keys of the returned Contributions must exactly match manifest `contributes`. */
  activate(ctx: PluginContext<Config>, info: ActivationInfo): Contributions | Promise<Contributions>;
  /** Idempotent. Process is killed at `reason.deadline` regardless. */
  deactivate?(reason: DeactivationInfo): Promise<void>;
  /** Only called when manifest lifecycle.reload.stateful = true. Serialized size ≤ 1 MB. */
  snapshotState?(): Promise<StateSnapshot>;
  healthCheck?(): Promise<HealthReport>;
  /** Omit to always reload on config change. */
  onConfigChanged?(next: Readonly<Config>, prev: Readonly<Config>): Promise<"applied" | "reload-required">;
}
export declare function definePlugin<Config extends JsonObject = JsonObject>(
  def: PluginDefinition<Config>,
): PluginDefinition<Config>;

/** open enum */
export type ActivationReason = "install" | "enable" | "upgrade" | "reload" | "restart" | "scale-out";
export interface ActivationInfo {
  readonly reason: ActivationReason;
  readonly previousVersion?: string;
  /** May be undefined even on reload; plugins MUST work without it. */
  readonly previousState?: StateSnapshot;
  readonly negotiatedApiVersion: PluginApiVersion;
}
/** open enum */
export type DeactivationReasonKind =
  | "uninstall" | "disable" | "reload" | "upgrade" | "scale-in" | "idle" | "shutdown" | "quarantine";
export interface DeactivationInfo {
  readonly reason: DeactivationReasonKind;
  readonly deadline: Date;
}
export interface StateSnapshot {

}

}

export interface Contributions {
  datasource?: Record<string, DatasourceProvider<any, any>>;
  transform?: Record<string, TransformProvider<any>>;
  visualization?: Record<string, VisualizationProvider<any>>;
  exporter?: Record<string, ExporterProvider<any>>;
  delivery?: Record<string, DeliveryProvider<any>>;

}

// ───────────────────────── Contexts ─────────────────────────
/** Instance-scoped. Available from activate() onward. No user authority. */
export interface PluginContext<Config extends JsonObject = JsonObject> {
  readonly plugin: { readonly id: string; readonly version: string; readonly installationId: string };
  readonly apiVersion: PluginApiVersion;
  readonly features: { has(feature: string): boolean };

  readonly config: Readonly<Config>;
```
